aggregate-entity.summary: The Cookie aggregate is in a substantially WORSE state than the round-3 RE-AUDIT claims: git history shows only E06 (PR #33, AggregateHydrator) merged into this branch, while PR #35 — which the RE-AUDIT marked as CLOSING F2/F3/F6/F7/F8/F9/F11 — was never merged. Verified against the live tree, none of those fixes exist: activate()/deactivate() raise no events, there is no softDelete()/restore() on the entity (lifecycle leaks through DeleteCookieHandler and RestoreCookieHandler+repository.restore()), CookieAccessors.php still exists with phantom @property ghosts, snapshot() is still a heterogeneous array, stock reason is still the stringly-typed method name, and CookieStockChangedEvent.cookieId is still ?int so the (int) cast in changeStock() is still wrong-direction. The one genuinely-landed improvement (E06 hydrator key + reconstitute version>=1 guard) IS coherent and correctly wired into CookieRepository::performSave. Beyond the stale-doc regression, the tree has live defects: a double-drain of pullEvents() between the repository and UpdateCookieHandler, an entire dead stock-mutation path (no DecreaseStock/IncreaseStock command handlers reach decreaseStock/increaseStock/assertPersisted), dead Shared/StateMachine code with zero call sites, and a User aggregate that diverges hard from Cookie (no AggregateRoot trait, no events, no optimistic-locking version, DateTimeImmutable vs string timestamps). This is the reference entity for dozens of ERP domains; cloning it today multiplies all of the above.
verified_fixed: F4 (reconstitute version=0): VERIFIED FIXED. Cookie.php:127-132 throws InvalidArgumentException when version<1, no default on the parameter. Landed via the E06/PR#33 merge (commit b04adcf).

F10 (no implements clause): VERIFIED FIXED. Cookie.php:55 'final class Cookie implements AggregateRootInterface'; AggregateRootInterface.php defines pullEvents/peekEvents/hasPendingEvents/getId. Landed via PR#33.

F5 (assignId/bumpVersion publicly callable with no guard): PARTIALLY FIXED and VERIFIED as landed. Cookie.php:157 and 175 now require an AggregateHydrator $key; AggregateHydrator.php has a private constructor and only key() mints one; CookieRepository.php:438,445,465 are the only call sites. Still convention-only until the E05.5 PHPStan rule lands (rule does NOT exist).

E06 integration coherence: VERIFIED. performSave (CookieRepository.php:425-468) bumps version to 1 then assignId on insert, and updateWithOptimisticLock then bumpVersion on update; in-memory version and DB version move in lock-step. The hydrator key is genuinely used, not decorative.

findings.title: Round-3 RE-AUDIT documents PR #35 fixes that were NEVER merged; F2/F3/F6/F7/F8/F9/F11 are all still open in the tree
findings.evidence: git log (b04adcf 'feat: merge E06 AggregateHydrator (PR #33)' is the last commit touching Cookie.php; no PR #35 merge commit exists). grep across app/ for CookieActivated|CookieDeactivated|StockChangeReason|CookieSnapshot|CookieStateAssertions|CookieLifecycle => 'NONE OF THE PR#35 ARTIFACTS EXIST'. RE-AUDIT-01 lines 22-31 claim these CLOSED via PR#35. Live Cookie.php contradicts every one of those rows (see sibling findings).
findings.impact: Any planning that trusts .audit/round3/RE-AUDIT-01-entity-aggregate.md will assume the reference aggregate is clone-ready when it is not. The remediation backlog is undercounted by ~7 findings. This is the single most dangerous gap: docs say 'done', code says 'not started', and Cookie is about to be cloned into dozens of ERP domains.
findings.fix: Treat RE-AUDIT-01 as aspirational, not factual. Either (a) recover/rebase the PR #35 branch and merge it, or (b) re-implement E07 from scratch (it is the source of most of these fixes). Re-classify F2/F3/F6/F7/F8/F9/F11 as OPEN in POST-REVIEW-CONSOLIDATED.md. Add a CI check or audit-discipline note that a finding is only 'closed' when the fix is on the default/stabilization branch, not when a PR exists.

findings.title: softDelete()/restore() do not exist on the entity; delete & restore semantics live in handlers + repository
findings.evidence: Cookie.php has no softDelete/restore methods (full file read, 332 lines; only isDeleted():bool at 328-331 and assertNotDeleted at 243-252). DeleteCookieHandler.php:92 dispatches new CookieDeletedEvent directly. RestoreCookieHandler.php:75 calls $this->repository->restore(...) then 95-101 dispatches new CookieRestoredEvent from the handler; its own docblock (lines 22-24) admits 'the entity does not yet expose a restore() lifecycle method'. CookieRepository.php:339-350 mutates deleted_at via a builder UPDATE.
findings.impact: The aggregate guards against the deleted state (assertNotDeleted) but cannot transition into or out of it — the core invariant 'who may change my lifecycle' is owned by the repository, not the aggregate. Every cloned ERP domain (invoice void, order cancel, inventory write-off) inherits this asymmetry: delete/restore events are raised from handlers, so audit trails depend on handler discipline rather than the aggregate. Soft-delete/restore cannot participate in the entity's event bag or outbox the way stock/update events do.
findings.fix: Implement E07: add softDelete(?Actor): void and restore(): void to Cookie that set/clear deletedAt and raiseEvent(CookieDeletedEvent / CookieRestoredEvent). restore() must reject a not-deleted entity (new ErrorCodes::COOKIE_STATE_NOT_DELETED). Rework DeleteCookieHandler/RestoreCookieHandler to call the entity method then repository.save() and let dispatchPendingEvents() drain — removing the manual dispatch and the bespoke repository.restore() builder UPDATE. Encode 'every lifecycle mutator raises >=1 event' in the domain-scaffolding skill so clones inherit it.

findings.title: activate()/deactivate() flip isActive but raise no domain event
findings.evidence: Cookie.php:306-316 — activate() and deactivate() each call assertNotDeleted() and set $this->isActive but never call raiseEvent(). No CookieActivatedEvent/CookieDeactivatedEvent classes exist (grep returned none). The class docblock (lines 36-39) only promises stock/update events are raised, so even the documentation no longer claims availability transitions emit events.
findings.impact: Activation/deactivation is exactly the business signal catalog/search/inventory consumers need. In a cloned ERP domain, the equivalent (publish/unpublish an item, enable/disable a price list) will silently toggle with no event, and the gap is rediscovered one consumer at a time. Also, these toggles are not idempotent-guarded (calling activate() on an already-active cookie would still no-op safely today only because no event fires).
findings.fix: As part of E07, route activate()/deactivate() through a single private setActive(bool) that, when the state actually changes, raises CookieActivatedEvent/CookieDeactivatedEvent (or one CookieAvailabilityChangedEvent). Make it a no-op (no event) when already at target state. Add the event class(es) under app/Domain/Cookie/Events/.

findings.title: pullEvents() is drained twice for the same aggregate (repository AND UpdateCookieHandler), an ownership/ordering hazard
findings.evidence: CookieRepository::save() at line 124 calls dispatchPendingEvents(), which at line 177 does $events = $cookie->pullEvents() and then writes the outbox (185-190) + dispatches in-process (199-201). UpdateCookieHandler.php:120 calls repository->save($cookie) and THEN at 126 loops 'foreach ($cookie->pullEvents() as $event) $this->eventDispatcher->dispatch($event)'. Because pull-then-clear is single-shot (AggregateRoot.php:71-77), the handler's second pull returns [] today, so the handler loop is dead code.
findings.impact: Two layers both believe they own event dispatch. Today it works only by accident of ordering (repo drains first). If a future refactor makes the repo stop draining, or a handler calls pullEvents() before save(), events either double-fire (duplicate side effects across the ERP) or vanish. For the reference template this ambiguity is the worst kind: cloners will copy whichever pattern they notice. The outbox-first design in the repo is the correct owner; the handler loop contradicts it.
findings.fix: Pick ONE owner. Recommended: the repository's dispatchPendingEvents() is the single drain point (it already does outbox-first). Remove the pullEvents()/dispatch loop from UpdateCookieHandler.php:122-128 (and audit other handlers for the same pattern). If instead handlers must own dispatch, remove dispatchPendingEvents() from save() and have the repo only persist. Document the chosen owner in the AggregateRoot trait docblock and the cqrs-architecture skill.

findings.title: decreaseStock()/increaseStock()/assertPersisted() are unreachable — no DecreaseStock/IncreaseStock command handlers exist
findings.evidence: find app/Domain/Cookie/Commands -type d => only CreateCookie, DeleteCookie, RestoreCookie, UpdateCookie. grep for DecreaseStock*/IncreaseStock* command dirs => 'no such dirs'. Cookie.php:274-291 (decreaseStock/increaseStock) and :257-266 (assertPersisted) therefore have no application-layer caller; only tests can reach them. CookieStockChangedEvent (entity-raised) thus never fires from a real command flow.
findings.impact: The stock-change event path — the showcase example in AggregateRoot.php's own docblock (lines 22-30) — is dead at the application layer. A cloner studying Cookie sees stock mutation + event as the canonical pattern but there is no command demonstrating the end-to-end flow, so the reference for 'mutator + event + outbox' is incomplete. assertPersisted() (and its wrong error code, see next finding) is reachable only from these dead methods.
findings.fix: Either add ChangeStock/DecreaseStock/IncreaseStock command + handler that load the aggregate, call the mutator, save() (letting dispatchPendingEvents drain), to make the reference flow real; or, if stock is only ever changed via the bulk update path, delete decreaseStock/increaseStock/assertPersisted and CookieStockChangedEvent to remove the dead surface. Do not leave a half-wired showcase in the template.

findings.title: assertPersisted() throws with COOKIE_STATE_DELETED for a not-persisted (id null) condition
findings.evidence: Cookie.php:257-266 — assertPersisted() builds DomainException::invalidState('Cookie', '<op> requires a persisted entity (id is null)', ErrorCodes::COOKIE_STATE_DELETED). ErrorCodes.php:53-55 has only COOKIE_STATE_DELETED=401 and COOKIE_STATE_CONCURRENT_MODIFICATION=402; there is no COOKIE_STATE_NOT_PERSISTED. RE-AUDIT claimed this CLOSED (403) via PR#35 — not in tree.
findings.impact: Any log filter or alert that splits on error code conflates 'entity was soft-deleted' with 'entity has no id'. A copy-paste into a cloned domain replicates the wrong-code-for-wrong-state mismatch and there is no correct constant to point cloners at. Low blast radius today only because the method is dead (see previous finding).
findings.fix: Add COOKIE_STATE_NOT_PERSISTED = 403 to ErrorCodes.php in the 400-499 range and use it in assertPersisted(). Bundle with E07. If decreaseStock/increaseStock are deleted instead, this finding closes with them.

findings.title: changeStock() casts $this->id to (int) and CookieStockChangedEvent.cookieId is still ?int (null -> 0)
findings.evidence: Cookie.php:299 — 'cookieId: (int) $this->id'. CookieStockChangedEvent.php:33 declares 'public ?int $cookieId' with a docblock (line 27) noting 'tightened in E04' (not yet done). assertPersisted runs before changeStock today, but the cast silently turns a null id into 0 if that guard is ever bypassed or copied without it.
findings.impact: A cloned domain that omits the persist guard ships stock-change events with cookieId=0, corrupting any downstream consumer keyed on the surrogate. The cast advertises a trust assumption rather than enforcing it. Combined with the dead-path finding, this code is both unreachable and unsafe.
findings.fix: Tighten CookieStockChangedEvent.cookieId to non-nullable int (E04). Drop the (int) cast in changeStock() and rely on assertPersisted() (or, better, a non-null id type once private(set)/PHP 8.4 lands) to guarantee non-null. Update the event docblock to drop the '?int / E04' caveat.

findings.title: CookieAccessors trait still exists and declares @property ghosts for fields it does not own
findings.evidence: app/Domain/Cookie/Entities/CookieAccessors.php still present (file read, 75 lines). Lines 18-27 declare @property ?int $id, CookieName $name, ... for state defined on Cookie, not the trait. RE-AUDIT line 28 claimed this file DELETED and inlined via PR#35 — false in tree (grep 'use CookieAccessors;' present at Cookie.php:58).
findings.impact: Rename drift: change a field name on Cookie (e.g. $isActive -> $active) and the trait's getters silently break only at the @property contract level, not at runtime, until a getter is called. Every cloned domain gets a parallel FooAccessors with a duplicated phantom-property contract — the worst-of-both-worlds pattern (split file + no real type safety). getId() also lives in the trait, so the AggregateRootInterface contract is satisfied from a trait whose property list is fictional.
findings.fix: Inline the 9 getters (~25 LOC) into Cookie.php and delete CookieAccessors.php (this is what PR#35 intended). The getters carry no logic. Ensure getId() remains and keep #[\Override] off (PHP does not require it for interface impls). Update the domain-scaffolding skill so clones do NOT generate a *Accessors trait.

findings.title: snapshot() returns a heterogeneous scalar map (bool/int/decimal-string/null) used as event payload
findings.evidence: Cookie.php:228-238 returns ['id'=>?int, 'name'=>string, 'description'=>?string, 'price'=>decimal-string, 'stock'=>int, 'is_active'=>bool]. This array is passed as previousState/newState into CookieUpdatedEvent (Cookie.php:216-222). RE-AUDIT line 31 claimed this replaced by a CookieSnapshot VO via PR#35 — not in tree.
findings.impact: Downstream audit consumers comparing two snapshots cross-domain need per-key type knowledge (string price vs int stock vs bool flag). Serialisation to the outbox/JSON is lossy/ambiguous (bool->0/1, decimal-as-string). Every cloned domain repeats the heterogeneity in its Updated event, making a generic audit-diff tool impossible.
findings.fix: Introduce a typed CookieSnapshot/CookieChangeSet readonly VO (E07/PR#35 design) with whitelisted keys and a stable serialisation, OR commit to an all-string representation. Use it in update() and CookieUpdatedEvent. Document the choice in the cloning skill so all domains use the same snapshot shape.

findings.title: decreaseStock/increaseStock pass the method name as the event reason (stringly-typed)
findings.evidence: Cookie.php:278 changeStock(..., 'decreaseStock') and :290 'increaseStock'; reason flows into CookieStockChangedEvent.reason which is a plain string (CookieStockChangedEvent.php:36). The event docblock (lines 23-30) even suggests free-text values like 'sale'/'manual_adjustment'. No StockChangeReason enum exists. RE-AUDIT line 29 claimed an enum landed via PR#35 — not in tree.
findings.impact: The reason encodes the operation (already implicit) rather than the business cause (SALE/RESTOCK/RETURN/ADJUSTMENT). Cross-domain analytics ('why did stock/quantity move?') cannot rely on a typed column. Cloned Order/Inventory domains will repeat method-name-as-reason. Low practical blast radius right now because the whole path is dead (see dead-stock-mutation-path).
findings.fix: Add a StockChangeReason backed enum (Sale|Restock|Return|Adjustment|InitialStock) under app/Domain/Cookie/ValueObjects (or Shared if generic), make changeStock accept it, require the (future) stock command handler to pass the business reason, and type CookieStockChangedEvent.reason as the enum. Bundle with the stock-handler work.

findings.title: Shared/StateMachine (StateMachine + State + InvalidTransition) has zero call sites — unused scaffold not wired to Cookie
findings.evidence: grep -rn 'StateMachine|new StateMachine|implements State|State::' app/ excluding the StateMachine dir => 'NO USAGES FOUND'. grep 'use App\\Domain\\Shared\\StateMachine' app/ => 'NO IMPORTS'. The three files (StateMachine.php 115 LOC, State.php 26 LOC, InvalidTransition.php 42 LOC) reference D5 and ERP lifecycles (draft/approved/posted) in docblocks but nothing implements State or constructs a StateMachine. Cookie's own lifecycle (active/inactive/deleted) is hand-rolled booleans + deletedAt, NOT a StateMachine.
findings.impact: The very abstraction meant to model ERP lifecycle states (draft -> posted -> cancelled — the prompt's stated target) is present but unproven: it has never been exercised by the reference aggregate, has no tests-via-usage, and Cookie demonstrates the opposite pattern (ad-hoc booleans). Cloners will either ignore StateMachine (and re-hand-roll states) or adopt an unvalidated abstraction. Either way the template gives two contradictory lifecycle stories.
findings.fix: Decide its fate before cloning: (a) PROVE it by modeling Cookie availability/deletion as a StateMachine (draft->active->inactive->deleted with allowed transitions) so the reference uses it end-to-end and E07 lifecycle mutators route through machine()->transition(); or (b) if Cookie's boolean+deletedAt model is the intended ERP pattern, delete Shared/StateMachine to avoid a misleading unused abstraction. Whatever is kept must be the single documented lifecycle pattern in the cqrs-architecture skill.

findings.title: User entity diverges hard from the Cookie aggregate contract (no trait/interface, no events, no version, DateTime vs string)
findings.evidence: User.php:58 'final class User' — no 'implements AggregateRootInterface', no 'use AggregateRoot' (grep for the trait returns only Cookie). User has no $version field and no optimistic locking; mutators update()/activate()/deactivate()/suspend()/changePassword() (lines 218-308) raise NO events — User events are dispatched from handlers (CreateUserHandler, UpdateUserHandler, DeleteUserHandler, ChangeUserPasswordHandler per grep). Timestamps are \DateTimeImmutable (User.php:71-73) vs Cookie's ?string. suspend(string $reason) ignores $reason (line 271-275). No User repository drains pullEvents (only CookieRepository:177 and UpdateCookieHandler do).
findings.impact: Two reference aggregates contradict each other. A team cloning 'the template' may copy User (no events, no optimistic locking, raw DateTime) for an ERP domain and silently lose audit events and concurrency protection — the exact failures Cookie's E06/E07 work is meant to prevent. The divergence also means AggregateRootInterface guarantees nothing across the domain layer (only one implementer). For an ERP foundation this is architectural rot that compounds per cloned domain.
findings.fix: Bring User onto the Cookie contract (or explicitly retire User as a reference): make User implement AggregateRootInterface + use AggregateRoot, add a version field with the AggregateHydrator-guarded bumpVersion/assignId pattern and reconstitute version>=1 guard, raise events from its mutators, and have the User repository drain via the same dispatchPendingEvents pattern. Reconcile timestamp representation (string vs DateTimeImmutable) across both. If User is intentionally legacy, mark it clearly and exclude it from the 'reference to clone' set in the cqrs-architecture/domain-scaffolding skills.

findings.title: AggregateHydrator key + reconstitute are enforced by convention only; the E05.5 PHPStan rule does not exist
findings.evidence: AggregateHydrator.php:38 '@internal', key() at 56 has private constructor so the type cannot be forged, BUT any namespace can still call AggregateHydrator::key() and then assignId/bumpVersion. The promised PHPStan rule (referenced at AggregateHydrator.php:24 and Cookie.php:48,151 as 'E05.5') is absent (grep for any such rule/usage returns only doc references). bumpVersion (Cookie.php:157-160) also has NO assertPersisted guard — it can increment version on an id-null entity.
findings.impact: The 'permission token' is documentation-grade safety today: a controller or handler can mint a key and drive identity/version. Cloners will replicate the pattern believing it is enforced. bumpVersion-before-assignId would push version 0->1, and reconstitute's version>=1 guard would then wrongly accept that object as persisted.
findings.fix: Land the E05.5 PHPStan custom rule that restricts AggregateHydrator::key() (and ideally assignId/bumpVersion) calls to *Repository namespaces, before scaffolding the next domain. Add 'if ($this->id === null) throw new \LogicException(...)' to bumpVersion() symmetric with assignId(). Document in AggregateHydrator that the key is a fence only once the rule exists.

findings.title: update() silently mutates and returns without an event when id is null, contradicting its own docblock
findings.evidence: Cookie.php:212-214 — 'if ($this->id === null) { return; }' after mutating name/description/price/stock/isActive (206-210), skipping the CookieUpdatedEvent raise at 216-222. assertPersisted() exists (257-266) but is NOT called by update() (only by the dead stock methods).
findings.impact: A legitimate create()->update()->save() flow (or any cloned domain doing the same) mutates state but loses the update event — audit trails silently incomplete. The behavior is inconsistent with stock mutators, which DO guard via assertPersisted.
findings.fix: Either gate update() with assertPersisted('update') so pre-persist update is a loud DomainException (consistent with stock and future lifecycle mutators), or queue the event and rewrite cookieId at persist time. Document the chosen rule in the class docblock. This is the residual of round-3 F1/N1.

findings.title: CookieCreatedEvent is dispatched by the handler, not the aggregate (split-dispatch model documented as canon)
findings.evidence: Cookie.php docblock lines 40-41 state CookieCreatedEvent is dispatched by the create handler because the payload needs the freshly-allocated id. CreateCookieHandler.php:105 dispatches new CookieCreatedEvent after save. So the aggregate raises update/stock events but NOT created/deleted/restored — a split model.
findings.impact: Cloners read the docblock and conclude split dispatch is intentional/canonical. It stems from the ?int $id=null lifecycle (id only known post-insert). Across the ERP this means 'created' events always live in handlers, breaking the otherwise-uniform 'aggregate raises, repository drains' story and complicating a pure transactional-outbox guarantee for creation.
findings.fix: Pick an architectural exit and document it: (a) UUIDv7 identity generated pre-persist so create() can raiseEvent with a real id; (b) a deferred whenPersisted() callback on the aggregate that the repo invokes with the new id; or (c) explicitly bless split-dispatch in the cloning skill and standardise it. E07/E16 (UUID/PHP8.4) are the natural homes.

findings.title: Mutators construct multiple DateTimeImmutable instances for the same domain moment (timestamp drift)
findings.evidence: User.php mutators each call 'new \DateTimeImmutable()' independently (e.g. incrementFailedLoginAttempts at 248 plus lockAccount at 317 within the same call). RestoreCookieHandler.php:99 builds a fresh DateTimeImmutable for restoredAt unrelated to the DB write timestamp. Cookie currently has no nowUtc() helper at all (timestamps are repository-managed strings), so a future E07 softDelete must avoid the same drift.
findings.impact: The persisted timestamp (deletedAt/updatedAt) and the event's occurredAt/restoredAt can differ by microseconds, so 'when did X happen' has two slightly different answers. Trivial individually but compounds into audit reconciliation headaches across an ERP where events and rows are cross-referenced.
findings.fix: Compute the moment once per mutator: $now = new \DateTimeImmutable(); reuse it for both the field write and the event payload. Provide a protected nowUtc() on the AggregateRoot trait (or a shared Clock) and standardise it so cloned domains and E07's softDelete/restore use a single timestamp per operation. A Clock abstraction also makes time testable.

aggregate-entity.fix_plan:
ORDERED remediation plan for the aggregate/entity dimension. Execute top-to-bottom; each step is self-contained.

STEP 0 (XS, do first) — Correct the record. In .audit/round3/POST-REVIEW-CONSOLIDATED.md and the E06/E07 tracking, mark F2,F3,F6,F7,F8,F9,F11 as OPEN (not CLOSED): git history proves PR #35 never merged (last Cookie.php commit is b04adcf, the E06 merge). Decide whether to recover the PR #35 branch or re-implement E07 fresh. Do this before any planning trusts the round-3 RE-AUDIT.

STEP 1 (S) — Inline CookieAccessors (closes cookieaccessors-phantom-properties). Move the 9 getters from app/Domain/Cookie/Entities/CookieAccessors.php into Cookie.php (keep getId() to satisfy AggregateRootInterface), delete CookieAccessors.php, remove 'use CookieAccessors;' at Cookie.php:58. Update domain-scaffolding skill to stop emitting an *Accessors trait. No behavior change; unblocks a clean entity.

STEP 2 (XS) — Fix the error code (closes assertpersisted-wrong-error-code). Add 'public const int COOKIE_STATE_NOT_PERSISTED = 403;' to ErrorCodes.php in the 400-499 block; use it in Cookie::assertPersisted() instead of COOKIE_STATE_DELETED.

STEP 3 (L) — Implement E07 lifecycle on the aggregate (closes lifecycle-leaks-into-handlers-repo, activate-deactivate-no-events; refines assertpersisted/snapshot/reason). On Cookie.php: add softDelete(?Actor $actor): void and restore(): void (set/clear deletedAt, raiseEvent CookieDeletedEvent/CookieRestoredEvent; restore() rejects not-deleted via COOKIE_STATE_NOT_DELETED — add that constant too). Route activate()/deactivate() through a private setActive(bool) that raises CookieActivatedEvent/CookieDeactivatedEvent only on real change. Add the new event classes under app/Domain/Cookie/Events/. Memoize $now = new DateTimeImmutable() once per mutator (closes now-not-memoized-microsecond-drift for Cookie). Then rewire DeleteCookieHandler.php (drop direct new CookieDeletedEvent at :92 -> call $cookie->softDelete() then repository->save()) and RestoreCookieHandler.php (drop repository->restore() builder UPDATE at :75 and manual dispatch at :95 -> call entity restore() then save()). Remove the bespoke restore() builder from CookieRepository.php:339-350 once unused.

STEP 4 (M) — Resolve event-dispatch ownership (closes double-drain-pullevents). Choose the repository's dispatchPendingEvents() (CookieRepository.php:175-202, already outbox-first) as the SINGLE drain point. Delete the pullEvents()/dispatch loop in UpdateCookieHandler.php:122-128 and audit every other Cookie handler for the same pattern. Document the owner in AggregateRoot.php docblock and the cqrs-architecture skill so clones inherit one model.

STEP 5 (M) — Make the stock path real or remove it (closes dead-stock-mutation-path; enables stockchanged-int-cast + stock-reason fixes). If stock is a first-class operation: add a ChangeStockCommand + handler that loads the aggregate, calls decreaseStock/increaseStock, then repository->save() (letting Step-4's drain dispatch CookieStockChangedEvent). Introduce StockChangeReason enum and pass the business reason. Tighten CookieStockChangedEvent.cookieId to non-nullable int and drop the (int) cast at Cookie.php:299. If stock is only ever bulk-updated: delete decreaseStock/increaseStock/assertPersisted from Cookie.php and delete CookieStockChangedEvent. Do not leave the half-wired showcase.

STEP 6 (S) — update() pre-persist policy (closes update-prepersist-silent-no-event). Replace 'if ($id===null) return;' (Cookie.php:212-214) with assertPersisted('update'), making pre-persist update a loud DomainException consistent with stock/lifecycle; document in the class docblock.

STEP 7 (M) — StateMachine decision (closes statemachine-dead-code). Either model Cookie's lifecycle (active/inactive/deleted) through Shared/StateMachine so the reference proves the abstraction and Step-3 mutators route through machine()->transition(); or, if boolean+deletedAt is the intended ERP pattern, delete app/Domain/Shared/StateMachine/*. Whatever survives becomes the single documented lifecycle pattern.

STEP 8 (M) — Enforce the hydration fence (closes internal-handles-not-enforced). Implement the E05.5 PHPStan custom rule restricting AggregateHydrator::key()/assignId/bumpVersion to *Repository namespaces. Add 'if ($this->id===null) throw new LogicException' to Cookie::bumpVersion() symmetric with assignId(). Land before scaffolding the next domain.

STEP 9 (L) — Reconcile the User aggregate (closes user-aggregate-divergence). Bring User.php onto the Cookie contract: implement AggregateRootInterface + use AggregateRoot, add $version + AggregateHydrator-guarded assignId/bumpVersion + reconstitute version>=1, raise events from mutators (or drive via outbox), drain in the User repository, reconcile timestamp type (string vs DateTimeImmutable) with Cookie, and either use suspend()'s $reason or drop it. If User is intentionally legacy, mark it and exclude from the 'clone reference' set in the skills.

STEP 10 (M) — CookieCreatedEvent split-dispatch exit (closes split-dispatch-created-event). With E16 (PHP 8.4) / UUIDv7 on the table, pick: pre-persist UUID identity so create() raises its own event, OR a whenPersisted() callback the repo invokes post-insert, OR formally bless split-dispatch in the cloning skill. Document the decision.

Sequencing note: Steps 0-2 are safe quick wins independent of the rest. Step 3 (E07) is the keystone and should precede Steps 4-7. Steps 8-10 can proceed in parallel once the entity shape is stable.
quick_wins: STEP 0: Re-classify F2/F3/F6/F7/F8/F9/F11 as OPEN in the round-3 consolidated report — git proves PR #35 never merged. Stops every downstream plan from trusting stale 'CLOSED' rows. (XS)
Add ErrorCodes::COOKIE_STATE_NOT_PERSISTED = 403 and use it in Cookie::assertPersisted() instead of the wrong COOKIE_STATE_DELETED (Cookie.php:263). (XS)

Add an id-null guard to Cookie::bumpVersion() (Cookie.php:157-160) symmetric with assignId() to close the version-before-id loophole. (XS)
aggregate-entity.erp_readiness_notes: CLONEABILITY CAVEATS when copying Cookie into real ERP domains (invoices/orders/inventory): (1) The reference aggregate is NOT in the state the round-3 docs describe — clone from the code, never from .audit/round3/RE-AUDIT-01. Until E07 lands, copying Cookie clones lifecycle leakage: delete/restore/created events come from handlers/repository, not the aggregate, so audit completeness depends on handler discipline in every domain. (2) Two contradictory reference aggregates exist: Cookie (events, optimistic locking via E06 hydrator, string timestamps) vs User (no events, no version, DateTimeImmutable). Pick ONE as the canonical reference and mark the other; otherwise teams will clone the weaker one and silently lose concurrency protection and events. This is the single biggest cloneability risk and overlaps the cloneability auditor's lane — flagging here as cross-cutting. (3) The AggregateHydrator key is convention-only until the E05.5 PHPStan rule exists; do not advertise it as enforced. (4) Shared/StateMachine is unused — ERP lifecycle states (draft/posted/cancelled) currently have NO proven pattern in the template; either prove it on Cookie or delete it before cloners pick an unvalidated abstraction. (5) The ?int id-null lifecycle forces split-dispatch for created events and motivates the (int) cast hazard; if ERP domains need created/posted events from the aggregate, plan UUIDv7 identity (E16) early rather than per-domain. (6) Event-dispatch ownership is currently ambiguous (repo AND handler both pull); settle it before cloning so all domains share one drain point — this borders the events/outbox auditor's lane. (7) Timestamp representation is inconsistent (Cookie string vs User DateTimeImmutable, and multiple now() constructions per operation); standardise a Clock/now-once rule so cross-referencing events and rows in the ERP audit log is reliable — this touches the platform-services/logging lanes.

value-objects.summary: The shared Money/Currency kernel is genuinely strong (integer minor-units, mandatory currency at every factory, PHP_INT_MAX overflow guards on string/float ingestion, currency-mismatch rejection, JsonSerializable wire format) and is the right foundation for ERP money. The problem is the Cookie wrapper that rides on it: CookiePrice still applies USD-cents bounds (1..999,999) to every currency and reports errors via hard-coded /100 arithmetic, so JPY/BHD catalogues are silently mis-bounded and mis-messaged (F1, the existential money defect E09 must fix). All three factories still accept ?Currency=null and silently cascade to env/USD (F2), undoing the very guarantee Money was hardened to provide. Money::multiply has no overflow guard (the one ingestion path the kernel forgot), which CookiePrice::multiplyBy and order-total math inherit. Beyond money: CookieStock has no max/overflow guard and a public $value read across the aggregate boundary, its docblock advertises a value() method that does not exist, and it has no dedicated unit test; CookieName equality is split between case-sensitive equals() and a raw-string equalsIgnoreCase(); the deprecated CookiePrice::format() symbol-override footgun is actively used in the read repository. Cross-domain, User VOs diverge sharply from Cookie: UserName throws raw \InvalidArgumentException (error code mis-passed as the PHP $code), so the error-code contract the HTTP layer relies on silently breaks for the User clone — a warning sign for every future domain. The Round-3 re-audit findings about CookieSnapshot/StockChangeReason/CookieChangeSet are verified fixed (those VOs were deleted).
verified_fixed: RE-AUDIT-02 N2 (CookieSnapshot public constructor): verified fixed — app/Domain/Cookie/ValueObjects/ now contains only CookieName.php, CookiePrice.php, CookieStock.php; CookieSnapshot.php no longer exists (confirmed via directory listing and find).

RE-AUDIT-02 N3 (StockChangeReason enum under ValueObjects with no boundary parser): verified fixed — StockChangeReason.php no longer exists under app/Domain/Cookie/ValueObjects (find returned nothing).
RE-AUDIT-02 N4 (CookieSnapshot::fromArray throwing \InvalidArgumentException via CookieChangeSet): verified fixed by removal — no CookieChangeSet / CookieSnapshot files remain in the Cookie VO tree.

Round-3 02 F1/F2 partial: CookiePrice now uses PHP 8.3 typed class constants (CookiePrice.php:22-23 `private const int MIN_MINOR_UNITS`), confirming the typed-const portion of the prior style work landed (the bounds-correctness portion did NOT — still open as vo-price-currency-blind-bounds).

findings.title: CookiePrice bounds and error messages are USD-cents semantics applied to every currency
findings.evidence: app/Domain/Cookie/ValueObjects/CookiePrice.php:22-23 define MIN_MINOR_UNITS=1 / MAX_MINOR_UNITS=999_999 with comment '9,999.99 in 2-decimal currencies'. assertPositiveAndInRange (lines 195-214) compares the raw $money->amountMinor() with no reference to $money->currency->decimals, and emits error 'actual'/'min'/'max' as $minorUnits/100 (lines 200-201, 208-210). For JPY (0 decimals) the ceiling becomes ¥999,999 (~$6.7k) and a ¥10000 price is reported as '100.00'; for BHD (3 decimals) the ceiling becomes 999.999 BHD. CookiePriceTest.php has zero JPY/BHD cases (only USD/EUR which are both 2-decimal), so the defect is completely untested.
findings.impact: Money correctness is existential for an ERP. Every cloned monetary VO (InvoiceLinePrice, OrderUnitPrice, ...) inherits a multi-currency-shaped wrapper whose validator and error messages are silently single-currency. A 0-decimal or 3-decimal currency catalogue is mis-bounded and the rejection message states a wrong number, which will be read by support staff and logged.
findings.fix: In E09: (1) Replace the two int constants with currency-aware bounds computed per call, e.g. derive max from a decimal string ('9999.99') via Money::fromDecimalString($maxDecimal, $money->currency)->amountMinor() so the cap scales with $currency->decimals; min should be the smallest representable unit (Money::fromMinorUnits(1, $currency)). (2) In assertPositiveAndInRange, build a throwaway Money for the offending amount and emit error context via $offending->toDecimalString() instead of $minorUnits/100. (3) Add CookiePriceTest cases for Currency::fromIso('JPY') and 'BHD' asserting both bounds and the decimal-correct error text. Do this in app/Domain/Cookie/ValueObjects/CookiePrice.php and tests/Unit/Domain/Cookie/ValueObjects/CookiePriceTest.php.

findings.title: All CookiePrice factories accept ?Currency=null and silently cascade env -> USD
findings.evidence: app/Domain/Cookie/ValueObjects/CookiePrice.php:42 (fromString), 70 (fromMinorUnits), 81 (fromFloat) all default `?Currency $currency = null` and fall through to self::defaultCurrency() (line 220-223) -> Currency::default() (Currency.php:103-114) which reads getenv('DEFAULT_CURRENCY') and silently returns Currency::usd() on missing/invalid input. Money.php:46-52 documents the exact opposite intent ('an implicit USD default would silently convert 1500 yen into $15.00'). Call sites CreateCookieHandler.php:81 and UpdateCookieHandler.php:96 call CookiePrice::fromString($command->price) with no currency, so creation is always env/USD.
findings.impact: CookiePrice re-introduces, one layer up, the footgun Money was deliberately hardened against. Cloning this for an intrinsically multi-currency aggregate (Invoice, OrderLine) copies a 'null -> getenv -> USD' cascade hidden inside a VO, plus a getenv() call buried in the domain layer (an impurity that breaks deterministic tests and hexagonal boundaries).
findings.fix: In E09: make $currency a required parameter on fromString/fromMinorUnits/fromFloat; delete defaultCurrency() from the VO. Push the default-currency decision to the use-case boundary: have CreateCookieCommand/UpdateCookieCommand carry an explicit Currency (or ISO string) resolved from request/settings, and pass it into CookiePrice::fromString($price, $currency). If a tenant default is needed, inject it via a SettingsService at the handler, not via getenv() inside the VO. Update CreateCookieHandler.php:81, UpdateCookieHandler.php:96, CookieRepository.php:392, and CookieQueryRepository.php:202 to supply the stored/explicit currency.

findings.title: Money::multiply (and CookiePrice::multiplyBy) has no PHP_INT_MAX overflow guard
findings.evidence: app/Domain/Shared/ValueObjects/Money.php:263-266 — `multiply(int $multiplier)` returns `new self($this->amountMinor * $multiplier, $this->currency)` with no bounds check. This contrasts with fromDecimalString (lines 89-104) and fromFloat (lines 133-138) which both explicitly guard PHP_INT_MAX. CookiePrice::multiplyBy (CookiePrice.php:161-167) and add/subtract delegate to Money, so a large quantity (e.g. line-item qty from a CSV import) silently wraps a 64-bit signed product into a small or negative amount.
findings.impact: Order/invoice line totals (price x quantity) are the single most common money operation in an ERP. A silent wrap to a negative total is a data-integrity/financial-loss bug that compounds across every domain that multiplies Money. The kernel guards ingestion but not the arithmetic path that actually overflows in practice.
findings.fix: In Money::multiply, after computing the product detect overflow before constructing: use a checked multiply (e.g. if $multiplier !== 0 && intdiv(PHP_INT_MAX, abs($multiplier)) < abs($this->amountMinor) then throw ValidationException::invalidFormat('amount', sprintf('a value within %s minor units', PHP_INT_MAX))). Add the analogous guard to add/subtract if totals can overflow. Add tests in tests/Unit/Domain/Shared/ValueObjects/MoneyTest.php for multiply overflow, and a CookiePrice::multiplyBy overflow test.

findings.title: CookieStock has no maximum and incrementBy can overflow to negative stock
findings.evidence: app/Domain/Cookie/ValueObjects/CookieStock.php:39-46 fromInt only rejects $value < 0 (no upper bound); incrementBy (lines 71-76) does unguarded `new self($this->value + $quantity)`. There is no MAX_STOCK constant. Repeated increments or a single large fromInt can reach PHP_INT_MAX and wrap negative, at which point isOutOfStock() (line 78-81, `=== 0`) returns false and decrementBy (lines 52-66) would compute against a negative base. Money guards this exact risk on its factories; CookieStock does not.
findings.impact: CookieStock is THE template for ERP inventory/quantity VOs (Inventory, OrderQuantity, Allocation). A silent integer wraparound to negative stock is a correctness/oversell vulnerability that every cloned quantity VO inherits. Also note Round-3 F4 flagged this and it remains fully open.
findings.fix: Add `private const int MAX_STOCK = 1_000_000_000;` (pick a domain-sensible ceiling). In fromInt, reject $value > MAX_STOCK with ValidationException::outOfRange('stock', 0, MAX_STOCK, $value, ErrorCodes::COOKIE_VALIDATION_STOCK). In incrementBy, compute $sum = $this->value + $quantity and reject $sum > MAX_STOCK before constructing. File: app/Domain/Cookie/ValueObjects/CookieStock.php.

findings.title: CookieStock::$value is public (read across aggregate boundary) and its docblock advertises a non-existent value() method
findings.evidence: app/Domain/Cookie/ValueObjects/CookieStock.php:32 `private function __construct(public int $value)`. The class docblock (lines 26-27) shows `$stock->value();  // 45` and `$stock->isOutOfStock();` as the usage contract, but no value() method exists in the file (grep for 'value()' returns only the docblock line 27). Callers read the property directly: app/Domain/Cookie/Entities/CookieAccessors.php:52 `return $this->stock->value;`, Cookie.php:235, Cookie.php:295, Cookie.php:301. CookieName (private + getValue()) and CookiePrice (private + getMinorUnits()) use the opposite encapsulation style.
findings.impact: Three sibling VOs present three encapsulation styles (public prop, private+getValue, private+getMinorUnits); cloners pattern-match the first they see. The docblock/code mismatch will make a cloner write $newQty->value() and get a fatal error, or copy the public-property leak. Direct $stock->value access also means a future invariant added to stock reads cannot be enforced.
findings.fix: Decide one convention for trivial VOs. Recommended: keep readonly but make $value private and add `public function value(): int { return $this->value; }` to match the docblock; then update CookieAccessors.php:52 and Cookie.php:235,295,301 to call ->value(). Alternatively, if public-readonly-prop is the chosen house style, fix the docblock (remove the () ) and apply the same style to CookieName/CookiePrice. Either way, document the rule in the cqrs-architecture skill.

findings.title: CookieName equality split between case-sensitive equals() and raw-string equalsIgnoreCase()
findings.evidence: app/Domain/Cookie/ValueObjects/CookieName.php:111-114 `equals(CookieName)` is strict `===`; lines 124-127 `equalsIgnoreCase(string $name)` lowercases both and re-trims the argument (receiver already trimmed at construction so that trim is dead). Docblock (line 119) says equalsIgnoreCase is 'useful for checking uniqueness', implying uniqueness is case-insensitive, yet the canonical equals() is case-sensitive. The string overload bypasses VO validation entirely (a 200-char or empty argument silently returns false instead of surfacing a malformed-name bug).
findings.impact: VO equality should be total and unambiguous. A cloner copies equals() believing it authoritative and ships records 'Chocolate Chip' and 'chocolate chip' as distinct. The raw-string overload leaks unvalidated input into business logic. Repository uniqueness semantics are split between two methods. (User domain's Email has the same shape via equalsString — UserName has none — so the inconsistency is already spreading.)
findings.fix: Pick one semantics. Recommended for names: case-fold on construction is risky for display, so keep display casing but make equals() compare a normalized fold (mb_convert_case($this->value, MB_CASE_LOWER)) and DELETE equalsIgnoreCase(); have the repository uniqueness check use equals() only. If a string overload must remain, route it through self::fromString($name) first so it cannot accept invalid input. File: app/Domain/Cookie/ValueObjects/CookieName.php plus the repository uniqueness call site.

findings.title: Deprecated CookiePrice::format() with arbitrary symbol-override is actively used in the read repository
findings.evidence: app/Domain/Cookie/ValueObjects/CookiePrice.php:125-131 `format(?string $currencySymbol = null)` is marked @deprecated (line 123, points at PriceFormatter::format) yet still concatenates an arbitrary $currencySymbol with toDecimalString() (line 130) — i.e. you can render a USD amount as '€2.99'. PriceFormatter.php:32-38 replicates the same override. app/Domain/Cookie/Repositories/CookieQueryRepository.php:202 calls `CookiePrice::fromString($decimalPrice)->format()` on the read path: it re-parses a stored decimal back into a CookiePrice (defaulting to env/USD, losing the row's real currency) purely to format it. CookiePriceTest.php:106-107,228-233 lock the override behavior into tests.
findings.impact: The read side mislabels currency: a stored non-USD price is reformatted with the env/USD symbol because the currency column is dropped during fromString. The deprecated symbol-override trapdoor will outlive its deprecation tag and get cloned. Presentation logic (symbol prefixing) is leaking back into the VO that PriceFormatter (E10) was supposed to own.
findings.fix: E10/E09: (1) Delete CookiePrice::format() entirely; route all formatting through the read model / a MoneyFormatter that takes amount_minor + currency from the projection row, not a re-parsed VO. (2) In CookieQueryRepository.php:202 format directly from the stored minor-units + currency (the projection should already carry both per E09's price_minor migration), not by rebuilding a CookiePrice. (3) Update/replace CookiePriceTest assertions on format(). Make PriceFormatter currency-faithful (never accept a symbol that contradicts the currency).

findings.title: CookiePrice::getValue(): float is dead code that re-introduces float drift
findings.evidence: app/Domain/Cookie/ValueObjects/CookiePrice.php:105-108 `getValue(): float` returns `$money->amountMinor() / (10 ** decimals)` — a float division that defeats minor-units arithmetic. Grep for `price->getValue()` / `->getValue()` filtered to price across app/ returns no production callers; only CookiePriceTest.php:24 asserts it. It is @deprecated (line 102).
findings.impact: A deprecated float escape hatch on the reference money VO will be cloned verbatim and called by developers who don't read the deprecation note, reintroducing rounding bugs in totals. Keeping dead code on the template normalizes float money access.
findings.fix: Delete getValue(): float from CookiePrice.php and remove the assertion at CookiePriceTest.php:24 (the line already asserts getMinorUnits() and toDecimalString() which fully cover the case). If any consumer truly needs a numeric, expose getMinorUnits(): int only.

findings.title: User VOs throw raw \InvalidArgumentException with the error code mis-passed as the PHP $code, breaking the error-code contract
findings.evidence: app/Domain/User/ValueObjects/UserName.php:55-81 throws `new \InvalidArgumentException('...message...', ErrorCodes::USER_VALIDATION_NAME)` — the second argument of \InvalidArgumentException is the PHP $code (int), NOT a domain error code, and there is no getErrorCode()/getErrors() structure. By contrast every Cookie VO and the shared Money/Email throw ValidationException (app/Domain/Shared/Exceptions/ValidationException.php:51-56 stores a distinct $errorCode and $errors map). So a UserName validation failure cannot be routed by the HTTP/error layer the same way a CookieName failure can: there is no field-errors map and no getErrorCode() accessor. AccessToken/PasswordComplexity/Email (User) DO use ValidationException, so within the User domain itself the pattern is inconsistent.
findings.impact: The Cookie reference says 'every domain VO throws ValidationException with a machine-readable error code + field map'. The User clone already violates it. When the ERP clones domains, whichever reference an engineer copies (Cookie vs UserName) determines whether the API returns a structured problem-detail or a bare 500/uncoded message. This is exactly the User/Cookie divergence the audit was told to treat as signal.
findings.fix: Rewrite UserName::fromString to throw ValidationException::required / fieldTooShort / fieldTooLong with ErrorCodes::USER_VALIDATION_NAME, mirroring CookieName.php:53-72. Audit all User VOs for any remaining raw \InvalidArgumentException throws and convert. Add a deptrac/PHPStan or test guard asserting domain VO factories throw ValidationException (or DomainException) — never bare \InvalidArgumentException. File: app/Domain/User/ValueObjects/UserName.php.

findings.title: Half the Shared VO kernel throws uncoded \InvalidArgumentException instead of ValidationException
findings.evidence: Within app/Domain/Shared/ValueObjects/: Currency.php:56-60 and 103-114, DocumentNumber.php:65-76, AttachmentRef.php:92-112, Actor.php:35-39, Permission.php:36-40, and RateLimitResult.php:33-39 all throw raw `\InvalidArgumentException` with no domain error code and no field map. Money.php and Email.php (Shared) throw ValidationException. So the shared kernel itself is split: a currency-format failure (Currency::fromIso) yields an uncoded exception while a Money amount failure yields a coded ValidationException.
findings.impact: These are the most-cloned building blocks (Currency, Money, DocumentNumber for invoice numbering, AttachmentRef for D11). An ERP that catches ValidationException at the boundary to build problem-details will let Currency/DocumentNumber failures fall through uncoded. The inconsistency teaches cloners that 'shared VOs throw \InvalidArgumentException' which contradicts the domain-VO contract.
findings.fix: Decide the kernel contract: either (a) all Shared VOs throw ValidationException with a shared error-code namespace (introduce App\Domain\Shared\SharedErrorCodes for currency/document/attachment/permission codes), or (b) explicitly document that structural-invariant VOs (Currency shape, DocumentNumber series) throw \InvalidArgumentException because they represent programmer errors not user-input. Recommended (a) for anything reachable from user input (Currency::fromIso, Permission::fromString), keep \InvalidArgumentException only for reconstitute() paths. Files: Currency.php, DocumentNumber.php, AttachmentRef.php, Permission.php, RateLimitResult.php.

findings.title: Two near-duplicate Email VOs (Shared and User) that have already diverged
findings.evidence: app/Domain/Shared/ValueObjects/Email.php and app/Domain/User/ValueObjects/Email.php both exist. They differ: User/Email.php:55-65 throws ValidationException::required + invalidFormat WITH ErrorCodes::USER_VALIDATION_EMAIL; Shared/Email.php:49-51 throws invalidFormat WITHOUT any error code and has no empty-string required() branch (an empty string fails filter_var so the message is 'invalid format' not 'required'). User/Email has equalsString (line 135) and uses explode for getDomain; Shared/Email has getDomain via strpos and no string-equality. All User-domain code imports App\Domain\User\ValueObjects\Email (8 call sites incl. UserRepositoryInterface, User entity); the Shared Email appears unused by the User domain.
findings.impact: Duplicate VO with drifting validation/error-code behavior is exactly what the shared kernel is supposed to prevent. When an ERP domain needs an email (Customer, Supplier contact) the cloner must choose between two Emails with different error-code behavior; whichever is copied propagates its (in)consistency. The Shared/Email's missing error code also means generic email failures are uncoded.
findings.fix: Consolidate to one canonical Email in App\Domain\Shared\ValueObjects. Give it a parameterizable or shared error code (or have it throw ValidationException with a Shared email code), add the required() empty-string branch, and the equals/equalsString surface. Repoint User imports (UserName-style 8 call sites) to the shared Email and delete app/Domain/User/ValueObjects/Email.php. Verify deptrac still passes (User -> Shared is allowed).

findings.title: CookiePrice::multiplyBy throws ValidationException without the price error code
findings.evidence: app/Domain/Cookie/ValueObjects/CookiePrice.php:163-165 `throw ValidationException::tooSmall('quantity', 1, $quantity)` passes no $errorCode (defaults to 0). applyDiscount (line 174-181) correctly passes ErrorCodes::COOKIE_VALIDATION_PRICE. CookieStock::assertPositiveQuantity (CookieStock.php:88-90) has the identical omission. So within a single VO some throws carry a code and some carry 0.
findings.impact: Handlers and the HTTP layer route on getErrorCode(); a 0 code is indistinguishable from 'unset'. A cloned VO copying this mixed pattern produces partially-routable errors. Round-3 F5 flagged this and it is still open.
findings.fix: Add ErrorCodes::COOKIE_VALIDATION_PRICE to multiplyBy's throw (or introduce a dedicated COOKIE_VALIDATION_QUANTITY constant in ErrorCodes.php and use it in both CookiePrice::multiplyBy and CookieStock::assertPositiveQuantity). Files: CookiePrice.php:163, CookieStock.php:89, app/Domain/Cookie/ErrorCodes.php.

findings.title: CookieStock has no dedicated unit test despite being the inventory-clone template
findings.evidence: find tests -iname '*CookieStock*' returns nothing; grep -rln CookieStock tests/ matches only CookieTest.php (entity), CookieServiceProviderTest.php, CookieEventHandlersTest.php — i.e. CookieStock is exercised only transitively via the entity. There is tests/Unit/Domain/Cookie/ValueObjects/CookieNameTest.php and CookiePriceTest.php but no CookieStockTest.php. The decrementBy negative-stock business-rule path, the assertPositiveQuantity path, isOutOfStock, and (once added) the MAX_STOCK guard have no direct VO-level coverage.
findings.impact: CookieStock is the reference for every ERP quantity VO, yet its invariants (negative-decrement DomainException, positive-quantity rule, future overflow guard) are only indirectly tested. The 90% coverage gate can pass via the entity tests while leaving the VO contract under-specified, so a clone may silently weaken a stock rule and still go green.
findings.fix: Add tests/Unit/Domain/Cookie/ValueObjects/CookieStockTest.php covering: fromInt rejects negative (and >MAX_STOCK once added), decrementBy below zero throws DomainException with COOKIE_BUSINESS_RULE_STOCK_NEGATIVE, incrementBy/decrementBy reject non-positive quantity, incrementBy overflow rejected, isOutOfStock at 0. (Owned jointly with the tests dimension — flag there too.)

findings.title: AccessToken::equals compares \DateTimeImmutable with === (object identity, not instant)
findings.evidence: app/Domain/User/ValueObjects/AccessToken.php:76-80 `equals` returns `$this->token === $other->token && $this->expiresAt === $other->expiresAt`. `===` on two DateTimeImmutable objects compares object identity, so two AccessTokens with the same token string and an equal-but-distinct expiry instant compare as not-equal. DateTimeValue.php:138-141 explicitly documents and fixes this exact pitfall by comparing getTimestamp(); AccessToken does not follow that lesson.
findings.impact: Latent equality bug; low blast radius today (token equality is rarely used) but it is a mis-pattern a cloner may copy into a VO where datetime equality matters. It also shows the DateTimeValue lesson hasn't been propagated.
findings.fix: Compare the expiry by instant: `&& $this->expiresAt->getTimestamp() === $other->expiresAt->getTimestamp()` (or wrap expiresAt in DateTimeValue and use its equals()). File: app/Domain/User/ValueObjects/AccessToken.php:78-79.

findings.title: No identity value object for aggregates (Cookie/User use raw int ids)
findings.evidence: find app/Domain -iname '*Id*.php' returns no CookieId/UserId VO (only query/handler files named *ById). Cookie.php:60 stores `private ?int $id = null`; GetCookieByIdQuery and accessors pass raw int. The shared kernel has Money, Currency, Email, DateTimeValue, DocumentNumber, AttachmentRef, Actor, Permission but no typed identifier VO.
findings.impact: For an ERP with dozens of aggregates, raw int ids invite cross-aggregate id mix-ups (passing an OrderId where an InvoiceId is expected compiles fine). A shared EntityId / typed-id pattern is a common DDD safeguard the template currently lacks, so every cloned domain repeats the raw-int approach. Lower severity because int ids are functional and a refactor is invasive.
findings.fix: Optional/strategic: introduce an abstract shared IdentityId VO (App\Domain\Shared\ValueObjects) or a per-aggregate readonly id VO (CookieId::fromInt) with equals(), and thread it through entity/commands/queries. Given the cost, scope this as its own epic rather than bundling into E09; document the decision either way so cloners know int ids are intentional.

findings.title: Sibling VO style drift: typed-vs-untyped consts, factory naming, encapsulation
findings.evidence: CookiePrice.php:22-23 uses typed consts (`private const int`); CookieName.php:39-40 uses untyped (`private const MIN_LENGTH = 3;`); UserName.php:35-36 and PasswordComplexity.php:30-35 use typed consts. Factory naming is mixed: CookieName::fromString, CookiePrice::fromString/fromMinorUnits/fromFloat, CookieStock::fromInt (named after the primitive, not a semantic source). Encapsulation is mixed (see vo-stock-public-value). Round-3 N1/F10 flagged these and they remain.
findings.impact: Three VOs in the reference directory present three styles; cloners copy the first they see, multiplying review noise across every ERP domain. Type-named factories (fromInt) set a precedent for OrderId::fromInt, CustomerAge::fromInt that lose semantic meaning.
findings.fix: Adopt one house style: typed class constants everywhere (add `: int`/`: string` to CookieName.php:39-40), and either keep fromInt or rename CookieStock::fromInt -> fromQuantity/of with the type-named one as an alias. Document the convention in the cqrs-architecture / domain-scaffolding skills so scaffolding emits it. Files: CookieName.php, CookieStock.php.

value-objects.fix_plan:
## Value Objects — ordered remediation plan

Execute in this order. Phases 1-2 are correctness (money/stock); phase 3 is the error-code/exception contract; phase 4 is cloneability/style; phase 5 is strategic.

### Phase 1 — Money correctness (existential; do first)
1. **(S) Add overflow guard to Money::multiply** — `app/Domain/Shared/ValueObjects/Money.php:263-266`. Before constructing, checked-multiply: `if ($multiplier !== 0 && intdiv(PHP_INT_MAX, abs($multiplier)) < abs($this->amountMinor)) throw ValidationException::invalidFormat('amount', sprintf('a value within %s minor units', PHP_INT_MAX));`. Add MoneyTest cases (overflow on multiply). This protects every line-total in the ERP. (finding vo-money-multiply-no-overflow-guard)
2. **(M) E09 — currency-aware CookiePrice bounds** — `app/Domain/Cookie/ValueObjects/CookiePrice.php:22-23,195-214`. Replace int constants with per-call bounds derived from `$money->currency` (max via Money::fromDecimalString('9999.99',$currency)->amountMinor(); min via Money::fromMinorUnits(1,$currency)). Emit error context through a throwaway Money's toDecimalString() instead of `/100`. Add JPY + BHD test cases to CookiePriceTest.php. (vo-price-currency-blind-bounds)
3. **(L) E09 — require explicit Currency on CookiePrice factories** — `CookiePrice.php:42,70,81`; delete defaultCurrency() (lines 220-223). Thread currency from the command boundary: update CreateCookieHandler.php:81, UpdateCookieHandler.php:96, CookieRepository.php:392, CookieQueryRepository.php:202. Remove the getenv() impurity from the domain. (vo-price-implicit-usd-default)

### Phase 2 — Stock correctness
4. **(XS) Add MAX_STOCK + overflow guard to CookieStock** — `CookieStock.php:39-46,71-76`. Add `private const int MAX_STOCK`, reject in fromInt and post-sum in incrementBy. (vo-stock-no-max-overflow)
5. **(S) Fix CookieStock encapsulation + docblock** — make `$value` private, add `value(): int` to match the docblock (lines 26-27), repoint CookieAccessors.php:52 and Cookie.php:235,295,301. (vo-stock-public-value-and-phantom-method)
6. **(S) Add CookieStockTest.php** — `tests/Unit/Domain/Cookie/ValueObjects/CookieStockTest.php` covering negative reject, MAX_STOCK reject, decrement-below-zero DomainException + error code, non-positive-quantity reject, increment overflow, isOutOfStock. (vo-no-cookiestock-test)

### Phase 3 — error-code / exception contract
7. **(XS) Add error code to multiplyBy + assertPositiveQuantity** — CookiePrice.php:163, CookieStock.php:89; consider new ErrorCodes::COOKIE_VALIDATION_QUANTITY in app/Domain/Cookie/ErrorCodes.php. (vo-price-multiplyby-no-code)
8. **(S) Convert UserName to ValidationException** — `app/Domain/User/ValueObjects/UserName.php:55-81`, mirror CookieName; add a test/PHPStan guard that domain VO factories never throw bare \\InvalidArgumentException. (vo-user-cookie-exception-divergence)
