value-objects.erp_readiness_notes: Money/Currency are the crown jewels here and are ERP-grade EXCEPT for three gaps that compound per domain: (1) Money::multiply has no overflow guard — price*quantity is the most common ERP money op and will silently wrap negative on large quantities; fix before any order/invoice domain is cloned. (2) CookiePrice mis-bounds and mis-messages every non-2-decimal currency (JPY/BHD) — do NOT clone CookiePrice for a multi-currency domain until E09 makes bounds currency-aware and removes the env/USD default cascade; the cloner will not notice the wrapper silently single-currencies their catalogue. (3) The error-code/exception contract is NOT uniform: Cookie VOs and Money/Email throw ValidationException with a code+field-map, but UserName and half the Shared kernel (Currency, DocumentNumber, AttachmentRef, Permission, RateLimitResult) throw uncoded \\InvalidArgumentException — whichever reference an ERP engineer copies determines whether the API returns a structured problem-detail or an uncoded error. Pick the canonical pattern and add a guard (PHPStan/test) before scaling domains. Cross-cutting watch-items for the entities/repositories/tests auditors: CookieStock::$value is read as a public property across the aggregate boundary (entity reads $stock->value directly) and has no dedicated VO test — both weaken the inventory clone. The read repository (CookieQueryRepository.php:202) re-parses a stored decimal into a CookiePrice purely to format it, dropping the row's real currency — this belongs to the read-side/E09 price_minor migration work, not the VO layer alone. Finally, there is no typed identity VO; for dozens of aggregates, raw int ids invite cross-aggregate id confusion — decide deliberately (typed Id epic vs documented intentional int) rather than letting each clone repeat the raw-int default by inertia.

read-side.summary: The Cookie read path is functionally correct and well-typed at the contract level (precise array-shape on findPaginated, narrowed read port returning CookieDTO, soft-delete + tenant filtering applied consistently, total/lastPage math has no off-by-one), but it is not ERP-ready and it carries a regression versus the round-3 re-audit. RE-AUDIT-04 claimed F3 (typed QueryHandlerInterface adopted) and F12 (CSPRNG LogSampler) were CLOSED; in this working tree they are NOT: there is no app/Domain/Shared/Bus/, no AbstractQueryHandler, no LogSampler, the three Cookie handlers implement no interface and still sample with mt_rand(), and QueryBus still duck-types handle() via method_exists with a @phpstan-ignore. Those fixes exist only in the unmerged stacked PRs (E05/E08), so every queries-handler finding from round 3 is OPEN here. The DTO/read-model slice (E10) was never even opened: CookieView is dead code (only its own file + test reference it), PriceFormatter is bypassed by 100% of production callers while CookiePrice::format() is @deprecated-pointing-at-it, dates flow through as raw MySQL DATETIME despite the DTO docblock promising ISO-8601, and CookieDTO carries behaviour (isOutOfStock()) and a nullable id. For ERP scale the search is the sharpest edge: $builder->like('name', $term) emits LIKE '%term%' (leading wildcard, unindexable) against a cookies.name column that has no index at all, guaranteeing a full table scan per search on every cloned domain. GetAll is unbounded, page has no ceiling (deep-OFFSET scan), and no read-side caching is wired despite the Cache infra existing. The User domain — the comparison signal — diverges sharply: it has no read port and hydrates the full write-side aggregate for reads, the exact cost CQRS read DTOs exist to avoid.
verified_fixed: Handlers return DTOs, not entities (round-1 CRITICAL): verified all three Cookie query handlers (GetCookieByIdHandler.php:54, GetAllCookiesHandler.php:52, GetCookiesPaginatedHandler.php:53) return CookieDTO/array<CookieDTO>/array-shape, never a Cookie entity. The read path goes through CookieQueryRepositoryInterface which returns DTOs only.

Read/write port split exists (round-1): CookieQueryRepositoryInterface (Ports/CookieQueryRepositoryInterface.php:27) exposes only findById/findAll/findPaginated returning DTOs; query handlers depend on it, not on the write-side CookieRepositoryInterface. NOTE: this is Cookie-only; User does NOT have this split.

findPaginated return shape is precise and total/lastPage are correct: CookieQueryRepository.php:157-163 returns array{data,total,page,perPage,lastPage} with $lastPage = max(1, ceil(total/perPage)); integration test CookieQueryRepositoryTest.php:76-79,128-134 pins total=5/lastPage=3 and empty=>lastPage=1. No off-by-one in the contract.

perPage is clamped to [1,100] in BOTH the query DTO (GetCookiesPaginatedQuery.php:43) and the repository (CookieQueryRepository.php:119); divide-by-zero on perPage is unreachable. Verified by tests test_find_paginated_clamps_per_page_to_one_when_zero / _to_one_hundred.

Soft-delete exclusion + tenant scoping applied on every read: findById/findAll/findPaginated all add where('deleted_at', null) and call applyTenantFilter() (CookieQueryRepository.php:70,90,123,129,72,97). Tenant isolation proven by CookieQueryRepositoryTest.php:158-195.
formatPrice swallows Throwable on malformed rows rather than 500-ing (CookieQueryRepository.php:199-208); proven by test_format_price_falls_back_to_raw_for_malformed_value.

findings.title: QueryHandlerInterface/LogSampler fixes claimed CLOSED in RE-AUDIT-04 are absent from this tree (regression vs re-audit)
findings.evidence: RE-AUDIT-04 closure matrix marks F3 'CLOSED' (interface adopted, method.notFound suppression gone) and F12 'CLOSED' (LogSampler/random_int). In the working tree none of that landed: `find app -path '*Shared/Bus*'` returns nothing; grep for AbstractQueryHandler/LogSampler across app/ returns nothing. QueryHandlerInterface exists only at app/Infrastructure/Bus/QueryHandlerInterface.php:20 as a marker (handle(object $query): mixed) and is implemented by NO Cookie handler. QueryBus.php:65 still does method_exists($handler,'handle') and QueryBus.php:96 still carries '@phpstan-ignore method.notFound'. git log --all shows AbstractQueryHandler/LogSampler live in commits 8a7a53b/34103df on the open E05 branch, not merged into stabilization/erp-foundation.
findings.impact: The structural guarantee that a cloned query handler cannot return a domain entity does not exist in the branch the ERP refactor builds on. A new domain can write handle(GetFooByIdQuery): Foo and the bus accepts it silently. The audit docs overstate the branch's maturity; an engineer trusting RE-AUDIT-04 would assume the seam exists.
findings.fix: Merge PR #34/#37 (E05) which add app/Domain/Shared/Bus/QueryHandlerInterface + AbstractQueryHandler, OR re-implement: (1) make QueryHandlerInterface generic (@template TQuery, @template-covariant TResult) and have all three Cookie handlers `implements QueryHandlerInterface`; (2) typehint it in QueryBus::register(string, QueryHandlerInterface) and delete the method_exists check + @phpstan-ignore at QueryBus.php:96. Resolve the stacked-PR conflicts first (base advanced).

findings.title: Paginated search uses LIKE '%term%' (leading wildcard) against an unindexed cookies.name column — full table scan per search
findings.evidence: CookieQueryRepository.php:136 calls $builder->like('name', $searchTerm). CI4 BaseBuilder::like (vendor/codeigniter4/framework/system/Database/BaseBuilder.php:1008) defaults $side='both', producing LIKE '%term%'. The canonical cookies table migration (2025-01-21-000001_CreateCookiesTable.php:130-134) indexes only tenant_id, is_active, deleted_at, and unique(tenant_id,name,deleted_at) — there is NO standalone or prefix index usable by the search, and a leading-% predicate cannot use a B-tree index anyway.
findings.impact: This is the canonical paginated-search shape every ERP domain (invoices, orders, inventory, customers) will clone. At ERP scale (100k-millions of rows) every search becomes a full scan; combined with countAllResults(false) the table is scanned twice per request. Direct production performance cliff multiplied across domains.
findings.fix: Decide the search semantics in the reference: (a) for prefix search use $builder->like('name', $searchTerm, 'after') => LIKE 'term%' and add an index on (tenant_id, name) so it is sargable; or (b) if substring search is a hard requirement, add a FULLTEXT index (MySQL) or a generated lowercased name_search column + index and document that the read model needs it. Add the index in a new migration; update CookieQueryRepository.php:136 and the class docblock. Document the chosen pattern in the cqrs-architecture skill so clones inherit a sargable search.

findings.title: Two competing read DTOs: CookieView is dead code while CookieDTO is canonical
findings.evidence: grep CookieView across app/ + tests/ returns exactly two files: app/Domain/Cookie/ReadModels/CookieView.php and tests/Unit/Domain/Cookie/ReadModels/CookieViewTest.php. Nothing in the production read path (controller -> handlers -> CookieQueryRepository) references it. CookieView.php:28 docblock calls itself 'the read-model DTO' while CookieDTO is the one actually wired. CookieView::detail()/summary() (lines 61,82) take a Cookie entity, so it is unusable from the row-based read repo anyway.
findings.impact: A cloner running the Cookie pattern produces both FooDTO and FooView and must guess which is canonical; the dead one accrues drift. The misleading 'read-model DTO' docblock points cloners at the wrong class. E10 is the planned fix but has not been opened, so this still ships.
findings.fix: Open E10. Pick CookieDTO as the single read DTO. Delete CookieView.php + CookieViewTest.php, or if its extra fields (version/deletedAt/isDeleted/isAvailable) are needed, fold them onto CookieDTO as precomputed fields and add a CookieDTO::fromRow(array) factory. Do not ship both. Update the cqrs-architecture/domain-scaffolding skills to scaffold exactly one read DTO per domain.

findings.title: PriceFormatter is dead-on-arrival: zero production callers while CookiePrice::format() is @deprecated pointing at it
findings.evidence: grep 'PriceFormatter::' across app/ finds only docblock examples in PriceFormatter.php:19-20. Both real formatting sites call the deprecated VO method: CookieQueryRepository.php:202 (CookiePrice::fromString(...)->format()) and CookieDTO.php:62 ($cookie->getPrice()->format()). CookiePrice.php:123 marks format() '@deprecated Use PriceFormatter::format()'. PriceFormatter::format (Services/PriceFormatter.php:32) and CookiePrice::format (CookiePrice.php:125) are near-identical wrappers over Money::format() / symbol-prefix.
findings.impact: The deprecation arrow points at a service nobody uses; cloners generate FooPriceFormatter + an equivalent @deprecated on FooPrice::format() and wire neither. Two parallel formatting code paths per domain with the 'authoritative' one unused. Self-contradictory reference.
findings.fix: Resolve under E10. Either (a) route CookieQueryRepository::formatPrice() and CookieDTO::fromEntity() through PriceFormatter::format($price) and drop @deprecated from CookiePrice::format() once unused; or (b) delete PriceFormatter.php and remove the @deprecated tag (the VO formatting itself is fine for one currency). Combine with the MoneyFormatter lift (see money-formatter-not-shared).

findings.title: CookieDTO date fields are raw MySQL DATETIME, not ISO-8601 as the docblock claims
findings.evidence: CookieDTO.php:31-32 docblock states 'ISO-8601 timestamp'. The read repo passes the column through verbatim: CookieQueryRepository.php:191-192 sets createdAt/updatedAt to (is_string) $row['created_at'] with no conversion. The cookies migration declares created_at/updated_at/deleted_at as type 'DATETIME' (2025-01-21-000001_CreateCookiesTable.php:112-123), and the unit test fixture confirms the wire shape '2025-10-21 10:00:00' (GetCookiesPaginatedHandlerTest.php:228) — a space separator, no 'T', no timezone offset. So serialized JSON emits a non-ISO-8601 string while the contract promises ISO-8601.
findings.impact: Every ERP API consumer cloning this DTO gets timestamps that violate the documented contract and break clients that parse strict ISO-8601/RFC-3339. No timezone marker means cross-region ambiguity. Multiplied across every dated field in every domain (invoices/orders are timestamp-heavy).
findings.fix: Under E10, introduce a shared date-to-ISO helper (the repo already has App\Domain\Shared\ValueObjects\DateTimeValue — add/use a toIso8601() conversion) and apply it in CookieQueryRepository::toDto() so createdAt/updatedAt are emitted as deterministic ISO-8601 with offset. Either fix the values or correct the docblock — values preferred. Cover with a test asserting the 'T' + offset format.

findings.title: GetAllCookies/findAll is unbounded — no LIMIT, no MAX_RESULTS safety net
findings.evidence: GetAllCookiesQuery.php (whole file, lines 16-27) has no MAX_RESULTS constant. CookieQueryRepository::findAll (CookieQueryRepository.php:86-107) emits no limit() — it array_maps every matching row into a CookieDTO. Handler GetAllCookiesHandler.php:52-63 returns the full array.
findings.impact: Cookie is presented as the canonical 'small reference list', but the template gives no signal that GetAll is dangerous. A cloned domain (AuditLog, Orders) with 500k rows OOMs the PHP process on the first GetAll call. Latent DoS replicated per clone.
findings.fix: Either delete GetAllCookies from the template (force the paginated variant), or add a MAX_RESULTS constant on the query, enforce it via limit() in findAll(), and log+throw when the row count would exceed it. Document that GetAll is only safe for bounded reference data. RE-AUDIT-04 maps this to the AbstractQueryHandler work (E08) but it is unmerged.

findings.title: Page number has a floor but no ceiling — deep-OFFSET scan via one querystring param
findings.evidence: GetCookiesPaginatedQuery.php:42 does $this->page = max(self::DEFAULT_PAGE, $page) with no upper bound. CookieQueryRepository.php:141 computes $offset = ($page-1)*$perPage and CookieQueryRepository.php:144 issues limit($perPage,$offset). page=999999999 yields LIMIT 20 OFFSET 19999999980; MySQL still walks the index to that offset.
findings.impact: Cheap DoS via ?page=, cloned into every paginated read in every ERP domain. LIMIT/OFFSET also degrades linearly with depth — already a problem before an attacker, for legitimately large lists.
findings.fix: Cap page at a sane absolute (e.g. MAX_PAGE = 10000) in the query constructor and throw ValidationException on overflow rather than silently clamping (surfaces client bugs). Longer term, document/provide keyset (seek) pagination for ERP-scale lists — see keyset-not-offered.

findings.title: Slow queries are logged at info, not warning — defeats alerting (Cookie diverges from User)
findings.evidence: All three Cookie handlers call $this->logger->info('Query executed', $context) even when $isSlowQuery===true, with slow_query only an extra context key: GetCookieByIdHandler.php:120, GetAllCookiesHandler.php:126, GetCookiesPaginatedHandler.php:136. By contrast the User domain does the correct thing: SearchUsersHandler.php:74-80 escalates to $this->logger->warning('Slow search query detected', ...). So the two reference domains disagree on the slow-query level.
findings.impact: Operators filtering level>=warning never see Cookie slow queries; the whole point of slow-query logging (alerting) is defeated. Cloned per-domain = silent perf cliff everywhere. The intra-repo inconsistency means cloners pick whichever reference they read first.
findings.fix: In each Cookie handler's logQuery, use $this->logger->{$isSlowQuery ? 'warning' : 'info'}(...). Best done once on AbstractQueryHandler (E08) so all clones inherit it. Align Cookie and User on the same level convention.

findings.title: Paginated search forces a log on every search regardless of queryLoggingLevel
findings.evidence: GetCookiesPaginatedHandler.php:84 — if ($isSlowQuery || $isSearchQuery) logs unconditionally, short-circuiting the queryLoggingLevel() match below. test_search_queries_are_always_logged_for_analytics (GetCookiesPaginatedHandlerTest.php:80-98) pins this behaviour even when level='errors'.
findings.impact: Operators who set queryLoggingLevel='errors' to silence noise still get a log line per search — at ERP scale (search-heavy admin UIs) this floods the operational channel. Cloned per-domain = systemic noise. Conflates analytics with operational logging.
findings.fix: Route search analytics to a dedicated 'search-analytics' channel (LoggerFactory::create('cookie.search')) instead of the operational logger, or gate it behind a separate searchLoggingEnabled config switch. Lift to AbstractQueryHandler so the seam is uniform.

findings.title: No read-side caching wired despite Infrastructure/Cache existing; no cache seam on the query path
findings.evidence: grep for Cache/remember/CacheInterface across app/Domain/Cookie + app/Controllers/Domain/Cookie returns nothing. app/Infrastructure/Cache contains only Services/CacheHealthCheck.php — no cache adapter, no decorator. The handlers have no cacheKey()/ttl hook (those exist only on the unmerged AbstractQueryHandler per RE-AUDIT-04). No event-driven invalidation path connects Cookie events to any cache.
findings.impact: GetCookieById and GetAll are obvious cache candidates for ERP reference data; adding caching later means touching every handler in every cloned domain. No documented invalidation contract (which event busts which key) means clones will either skip caching or invent incoherent ad-hoc caches.
findings.fix: Land AbstractQueryHandler's cacheKey()/cacheTtlSeconds() hooks (E08) and implement the cache check in the base; add a CachedQueryHandlerDecorator as the opt-in seam. Document the invalidation contract: CookieUpdated/Deleted/Restored/StockChanged events bust the per-id and list keys. Provide one worked example on Cookie so clones copy a coherent pattern.

findings.title: GetCookieById null-on-miss has no structural contract; controller silently redirects
findings.evidence: GetCookieByIdHandler.php:54 returns ?CookieDTO with docblock 'Controller can decide how to handle not found cases' (lines 27-29). The controller chooses a flash-redirect: CookieController.php:89-92 (show) and :176-179 (edit) redirect('/cookies')->with('error',...). No 404/NotFoundException is raised; nothing in the template commits to a single not-found semantic.
findings.impact: The reference leaves the most common read decision (what does 'not found' mean?) unanswered structurally. Cloned domains will each choose differently (404 vs redirect vs empty view), producing inconsistent API/UX across the ERP. An API clone returning a flash redirect for a missing resource is wrong.
findings.fix: Pick one in the template: keep nullable DTO AND show an API controller throwing PageNotFoundException()/returning 404 for the JSON path, plus the web redirect for the HTML path; document the split. Resolve under E10 alongside the ReadDTOInterface so the API envelope has a defined not-found shape.

findings.title: CookieDTO::id is nullable though the read path always produces an int id
findings.evidence: CookieDTO.php:35 declares public ?int $id. The read repo always casts (int) $row['id'] (CookieQueryRepository.php:184), so a read-reconstituted DTO never has null id. Views render $cookie->id directly into URLs (index.php:47,65,66). The nullable type permits a /cookies/ (empty) URL without a static-analysis warning. fromEntity (CookieDTO.php:55-67) passes $cookie->getId() which is the only legitimate null source (unpersisted entity).
findings.impact: A cloner can ship a read DTO whose id is null and only discover it at runtime when a URL renders empty. Read DTOs reconstituted from a row always have an id; declaring it nullable creates a contract that does not match the read reality and weakens link-building safety across every cloned listing/detail view.
findings.fix: Under E10, make the read DTO id non-nullable (public int $id). If a pre-persistence preview path genuinely needs null, give it a separate UnpersistedCookieDTO or only allow int|null at that construction site, not on the canonical read DTO. fromEntity then asserts getId() !== null before constructing.

findings.title: CookieDTO exposes a domain predicate (isOutOfStock()), blurring the DTO boundary
findings.evidence: CookieDTO.php:77-80 defines isOutOfStock(): bool returning $this->stock === 0, contradicting the class docblock 'Prevents domain entities from leaking into the presentation layer' (CookieDTO.php:11). Both views call it: index.php:52 and show.php:47.
findings.impact: Cloners see the precedent and add isLowStock()/isExpensive()/isOnSale() to FooDTO, growing it into a parallel entity and defeating the decoupling claim. The DTO/entity boundary the read side exists to keep clean is already leaking in the reference.
findings.fix: Replace the method with a precomputed public bool $outOfStock populated in CookieQueryRepository::toDto()/CookieDTO::fromEntity(); update the two views to read $cookie->outOfStock. Document in the skill that read DTOs carry data, not behaviour. Bundle into E10.

findings.title: No shared read-DTO serialization contract (toArray/JsonSerializable, snake_case, ISO dates)
findings.evidence: CookieDTO has no toArray() and does not implement JsonSerializable (CookieDTO.php whole file) — JSON would fall back to public-property reflection emitting camelCase keys (formattedPrice, isActive). CookieView::toArray() emits snake_case (is_active, is_deleted) (CookieView.php:103-119) but is dead. grep confirms no ReadDTOInterface and no JsonSerializable anywhere under app/Domain/Cookie. The CookieView docblock references an 'ApiResponse envelope' (CookieView.php:26) that does not exist in the read path.
findings.impact: A cloner copying CookieDTO ships camelCase JSON; copying CookieView ships snake_case; copying both ships both. No shared key-case or date convention means every ERP domain's API drifts. The referenced ApiResponse envelope is vapor.
findings.fix: Create app/Domain/Shared/DTOs/ReadDTOInterface with toArray(): array<string,scalar|null> + jsonSerialize(): array; standardize snake_case at the JSON boundary and ISO-8601 dates (reuse the date helper from dto-dates-not-iso8601). Have CookieDTO implement it. This is the explicit E10 scope (CookieDTO + JsonSerializable + ReadDTOInterface + MoneyFormatter).

findings.title: Price formatting is symbol-prefix only (no locale/Intl) and not lifted to a shared MoneyFormatter
findings.evidence: Money::format() (app/Domain/Shared/ValueObjects/Money.php:167-171) is $sign . $currency->symbol . $absStr — no NumberFormatter, no thousands separator, no locale. PriceFormatter::format (Services/PriceFormatter.php:32-38) and CookiePrice::format (CookiePrice.php:125-131) both reduce to that. Output is 'R$1234.5' rather than 'R$ 1.234,50'. PriceFormatter is Cookie-scoped (final, not even readonly) so each cloned domain gets its own copy.
findings.impact: Cloners assume PriceFormatter is locale-aware and ship it to production; ERP money display for BR/EU customers is wrong. Per-domain copies of an 8-line static method instead of one shared formatter; multiplied across invoices/orders/inventory.
findings.fix: Under E10, lift to app/Domain/Shared/Services/MoneyFormatter::format(Money $m, ?string $symbol=null); either upgrade to IntlNumberFormatter::CURRENCY with locale + currency code, or rename to honestly reflect symbol-prefix. Route CookieDTO/CookieQueryRepository through it and retire the Cookie-local PriceFormatter + CookiePrice::format() deprecation. Document the formatter as the canonical money-display seam for all domains.

findings.title: Read side offers only LIMIT/OFFSET pagination; no keyset/cursor option for ERP-scale lists
findings.evidence: CookieQueryRepository.php:141-144 implements offset pagination only (orderBy('id','ASC')->limit($perPage,$offset)); grep for cursor/keyset/seek across app/Domain/Cookie + app/Infrastructure returns nothing. The fixed orderBy('id','ASC') is stable (good for keyset) but no after-id seek path is exposed on the port or query.
findings.impact: OFFSET pagination scans+discards all preceding rows; on million-row ERP tables, page 5000 is a multi-second scan. The reference gives clones no keyset example, so every large-list domain inherits a pattern that degrades linearly with depth. countAllResults on every page compounds it.
findings.fix: Add an optional keyset variant to the read port (e.g. findAfter(?int $afterId, int $limit, ...)) returning {data, nextCursor} and demonstrate it once on Cookie; keep offset for small/admin lists. Document when to use which (offset for bounded reference data, keyset for unbounded transactional tables) in the cqrs-architecture skill. Decouple total-count from the hot path (lazy/approximate count).

findings.title: User read side hydrates the full write-aggregate (no read port) — opposite of Cookie's CQRS read split
findings.evidence: User has no UserQueryRepositoryInterface and no query repository (find app/Domain/User/Ports + Repositories shows only UserRepositoryInterface/UserRepository). GetUserByIdHandler.php:31-39 injects the WRITE port UserRepositoryInterface, calls findById returning a full User entity, then maps UserDTO::fromEntity($user) in the handler. SearchUsersHandler.php:63-90 calls the write repo's findPaginated (returns array<User> entities) and array_maps to UserDTO in the handler; it also mutates the result array shape (rename totalPages->lastPage at :92-93). Cookie's interface returns DTOs straight from rows (Ports/CookieQueryRepositoryInterface.php:27).
findings.impact: The template ships TWO contradictory read-side reference implementations: Cookie (separate read port, DTOs from rows, skips reconstitution) and User (write port, full aggregate reconstitution per row, map-in-handler). A cloner copying User inherits the exact entity-hydration-for-lists cost CQRS read DTOs exist to avoid, plus the SearchUsers result-shape munging. This is architectural rot that compounds per cloned domain.
findings.fix: Designate Cookie as THE read-side reference and bring User into line: add UserQueryRepositoryInterface returning UserDTO from rows, point GetUserById/GetAllUsers/SearchUsers handlers at it, and stop reconstituting User aggregates for reads. Standardize the paginated return shape (lastPage, not totalPages) across both domains. Until then, document loudly that User's read side is NOT the pattern to clone.

findings.title: GetAllCookiesQuery docblock contradicts its includeInactive parameter
findings.evidence: GetAllCookiesQuery.php:10-13 docblock says 'Returns all cookies that are: Active (is_active = true), Not deleted' while the constructor (line 23-25) takes bool $includeInactive = false. The 'Active' claim is false when includeInactive=true.
findings.impact: Cloners copy the docblock and forget to update it for includeArchived/includeInactive variants; the reference's own docs lie about behaviour. Low but it is the reference everyone reads first.
findings.fix: Rewrite to: 'Returns all non-deleted cookies. Excludes inactive by default; pass includeInactive=true to include is_active=false rows.' Trivial edit to GetAllCookiesQuery.php.

findings.title: Logging context hard-codes 'Cookie' domain and query-class strings (two sources of truth)
findings.evidence: GetCookieByIdHandler.php:109-110, GetAllCookiesHandler.php:115-116, GetCookiesPaginatedHandler.php:119-120 all set 'domain' => 'Cookie' and 'query' => 'GetXxxQuery' as string literals. The query name duplicates the class name. shouldSample() at GetCookieByIdHandler.php:130 (and the two siblings) still uses mt_rand()/mt_getrandmax() rather than a CSPRNG.

read-side.fix_plan:
## Read-side remediation plan (ordered)

Premise: this branch lacks the E05/E08 query-handler infrastructure that RE-AUDIT-04 assumed merged, and E10 (read DTO/serialization) was never opened. Sequence below resolves the regression first, then the ERP-scale performance edges, then the DTO/serialization consolidation, then cross-domain alignment.

### Phase A — restore the query-handler contract (regression first)
1. Resolve merge conflicts on PR #34/#37 (E05) and merge, OR re-add by hand:
   - Create `app/Domain/Shared/Bus/QueryHandlerInterface.php` generic (`@template TQuery`, `@template-covariant TResult`).
   - Make GetCookieByIdHandler / GetAllCookiesHandler / GetCookiesPaginatedHandler `implements QueryHandlerInterface`.
   - In `app/Infrastructure/Bus/QueryBus.php:57` typehint `register(string, QueryHandlerInterface)`; delete the `method_exists` check (lines 65-69) and the `@phpstan-ignore method.notFound` at line 96.
   - Effort: M.
2. Merge/re-add E08 `AbstractQueryHandler` + `LogSampler` (PR #36) and migrate the three Cookie handlers onto it. This single base then resolves, in one place:
   - slow-query escalation to `warning` (replaces the `info` calls at GetCookieByIdHandler.php:120 / GetAllCookiesHandler.php:126 / GetCookiesPaginatedHandler.php:136),
   - `random_int` sampling (replaces `mt_rand()` at GetCookieByIdHandler.php:130 + siblings),
   - derive `'query'` from `$query::class` + a `DOMAIN` const (removes literals at lines 109-110/115-116/119-120),
   - `cacheKey()` / `cacheTtlSeconds()` seam,
   - bounded `GetAll` via a `MAX_RESULTS` hook.
   - Move the search-analytics force-log (GetCookiesPaginatedHandler.php:84) to a dedicated channel/flag on the base.
   - Effort: M-L.

### Phase B — ERP-scale read performance (do before cloning)
3. Fix search sargability: change `CookieQueryRepository.php:136` to prefix search (`like('name',$term,'after')`) and add an index on `(tenant_id, name)` in a new migration; or commit to FULLTEXT/`name_search` generated column + index if substring search is required. Update the class docblock and the cqrs-architecture skill. Effort: M.
4. Cap `page` in `GetCookiesPaginatedQuery.php:42` (add `MAX_PAGE`, throw `ValidationException` on overflow). Effort: S.
5. Add a keyset/cursor read path on the port (`findAfter(?int $afterId, int $limit, ...)`) and demonstrate it once on Cookie; document offset-vs-keyset guidance. Decouple total-count from the hot path. Effort: L.
6. Wire read-side caching: implement `AbstractQueryHandler::cacheKey()` against a cache adapter, add a `CachedQueryHandlerDecorator`, and document event-driven invalidation (CookieUpdated/Deleted/Restored/StockChanged bust per-id + list keys). Effort: M.

### Phase C — read DTO + serialization consolidation (open E10)
7. Delete `CookieView.php` + `CookieViewTest.php` (dead). If version/deletedAt/isDeleted/isAvailable are needed, fold them as precomputed fields onto CookieDTO and add `CookieDTO::fromRow(array)`. Effort: M.
8. Create `app/Domain/Shared/DTOs/ReadDTOInterface` (`toArray(): array<string,scalar|null>` + `jsonSerialize()`); have CookieDTO implement it; standardize snake_case JSON. Effort: M.
9. Add a shared date-to-ISO helper (extend `App\Domain\Shared\ValueObjects\DateTimeValue`) and apply it in `CookieQueryRepository::toDto()` (CookieQueryRepository.php:191-192) so createdAt/updatedAt are ISO-8601 with offset; fixes the false docblock at CookieDTO.php:31-32. Effort: S.
10. Make CookieDTO::id non-nullable (CookieDTO.php:35); assert in fromEntity. Effort: S.
11. Replace CookieDTO::isOutOfStock() (CookieDTO.php:77) with a precomputed `public bool $outOfStock`; update views index.php:52 / show.php:47. Effort: S.
12. Lift price formatting to `app/Domain/Shared/Services/MoneyFormatter` (Intl currency or honest rename); route CookieDTO + CookieQueryRepository::formatPrice through it; delete Cookie-local PriceFormatter and remove the `@deprecated` on CookiePrice::format() (CookiePrice.php:123). Effort: M.
13. Commit a single not-found semantic for GetCookieById (404 for API, redirect for HTML) and document it. Effort: S.

### Phase D — cross-domain alignment (cloneability)
14. Bring User's read side onto the Cookie pattern: add `UserQueryRepositoryInterface` returning UserDTO from rows; repoint GetUserById/GetAllUsers/SearchUsers handlers; stop reconstituting User aggregates for reads; standardize the paginated shape on `lastPage` (remove the totalPages rename at SearchUsersHandler.php:92-93). Until done, annotate User handlers as NOT the reference pattern. Effort: L.
15. Decide the projection story: add a `registerProjections(ProjectionRegistry)` hook to the service-provider interface (even if Cookie registers none) and one end-to-end projection test, OR document the projection infra as opt-in and remove the stale `registerEvents()` re-enable note from the .example. Effort: M.

### Phase E — verification
16. Run phpstan L8 + phpcs + phpunit (90% gate) and deptrac after each phase. Update RE-AUDIT-04/07 closure matrices to reflect actual tree state (the regression note).
quick_wins: Fix the misleading GetAllCookiesQuery docblock (GetAllCookiesQuery.php:10-13) to match the includeInactive parameter — XS.
Fix or correct the CookieDTO ISO-8601 date claim: either convert dates in CookieQueryRepository::toDto() (lines 191-192) or fix the docblock (CookieDTO.php:31-32) — S.
Change CookieQueryRepository.php:136 search to prefix (like(..,'after')) to stop the guaranteed leading-wildcard full scan, even before adding the index — XS code change, big perf win.
Make CookieDTO::id non-nullable (CookieDTO.php:35) — the read path never produces null — S.
Cap page in GetCookiesPaginatedQuery.php:42 with a MAX_PAGE constant to kill the cheap deep-OFFSET DoS — S.
Delete dead CookieView.php + CookieViewTest.php (only self-references) to remove the two-competing-DTOs trap before anyone clones it — S.
read-side.erp_readiness_notes: When cloning Cookie's read side into real ERP domains, watch these: (1) The CookieQueryRepository read-port-returns-DTOs pattern is the GOOD reference — clone that, NOT User's GetUserById/SearchUsers which hydrate the full write aggregate via the write port; the two diverge and only one is CQRS-correct. (2) The search is the single most dangerous thing to clone: LIKE '%term%' on an unindexed name column is a full scan that will melt at invoice/order scale — fix the reference before it propagates. (3) Offset-only pagination + countAllResults on every page does not scale to transactional tables; provide a keyset path before cloning into high-volume domains. (4) Dates emitted as raw MySQL DATETIME (not ISO-8601) will break strict API consumers across every cloned domain — establish the shared ISO date + ReadDTOInterface (snake_case) contract first so all domains serialize identically. (5) Slow-query log level is inconsistent between Cookie (info, wrong) and User (warning, right) — pick warning and bake it into the shared base so clones inherit alerting. (6) The projection registry is wired but feeds nothing; it is fine that Cookie collapsed its read model, but the .example references a registerProjections hook that does not exist — any ERP domain that truly needs a denormalised read model has no executable, tested path to follow yet. Cross-cutting items outside my lane noted for the owning auditors: the read-side schema lacks a search index (schema auditor); CookieView vs CookieDTO and DateTimeValue/Money serialization belong jointly to the entities/VO auditors; the QueryBus duck-typing + @phpstan-ignore is a write/bus-infra concern; tenant filtering correctness should be confirmed by the auth/security auditor.

supporting-sweep.summary: Breadth-first sweep of all nine supporting dimensions (A-I). The single most damaging issue is in LOGGING/TESTS: integration tests run against a live SQLite DB with logging pointed at the real writable/logs/, and the UsersEmailUniqueWithSoftDelete migration's dropKey('users','users_email') throws "no such index: users_email" on SQLite, which the CI4 exception handler logs at ERROR on every test that migrates — producing a 389MB log-2026-05-22.log with ~92,746 copies of that one exception, plus a parallel 76MB Monolog app-*.json stream. Two complete logging stacks run in parallel (CI4-native log-*.log at threshold=9, and Monolog app-*.json), neither isolated under CI_ENVIRONMENT=testing. The good news: PR #42 (E18) explicitly targets "logger isolation + sleep removal", so the critical item is already in flight (with conflicts). SCHEMA, AUTH, and PLATFORM-DI are in much better shape than round-3 implied: the cookies table already carries tenant_id/version/created_by, the event_outbox DDL matches the E12 plan, the documented JWT/rate-limit/authorization security gaps are FIXED (prod startup guard, real .env secret, wired middleware, gitleaks job in CI), and tenancy is genuinely injected into Cookie repos in production via #[AutoBind]. The dominant remaining theme is HYGIENE-THAT-CLONES: empty app/Filters with three competing middleware homes, Commands+Helpers outside PHPStan/coverage scope, a duplicate dual test tree (PascalCase real + lowercase stubs), tenancy untested at the integration-base level, document numbering not tenant-scoped, and two tracked root audit .md files. DEPTH NOTE: this was a breadth sweep — areas C (views/i18n), F-mechanism, and E-service-ranking were spot-checked not exhaustively traced, so they are NOT certified clean; the write/read/event core is owned by the six deep auditors.

findings.title: Integration tests log to real writable/logs and spam 92,746 'no such index: users_email' ERRORs -> 389MB/day log
findings.evidence: writable/logs/log-2026-05-22.log is 389MB for one day; `grep -c users_email` = 92,746 and sample line: 'ERROR ... SQLite3Exception: no such index: users_email in vendor/.../SQLite3/Connection.php:175'. Root cause: app/Database/Migrations/2026-05-20-210000_UsersEmailUniqueWithSoftDelete.php:40 calls $this->forge->dropKey('users','users_email',false) but on SQLite the column-level UNIQUE from CreateUsersTable.php:23 ('unique'=>true) is NOT named users_email, so the drop emits a failing statement the CI4 handler logs at ERROR. tests/Support/IntegrationTestCase.php:32,39 set $migrate=true/$refresh=true (migrate every test) and :60-62 build a LoggerFactory logger; LoggerFactory::getLogDirectory() (app/Infrastructure/Logging/LoggerFactory.php:75-82) keys only off WRITEPATH, never CI_ENVIRONMENT, so logs land in the real writable/logs even under testing. Config\Logger::$threshold=9 in non-prod (app/Config/Logger.php:42) captures everything.
findings.impact: Every cloned ERP domain that copies IntegrationTestCase will (a) pollute real logs during CI/local runs, (b) inherit the same per-test migration cost, and (c) bury genuine errors under hundreds of thousands of benign exception lines. A 389MB/76MB-per-day log pair will fill disks on CI runners and dev machines and makes the Monolog 'AI-readable logs' premise unusable. The dropKey-on-nonexistent-index pattern also re-fires on every clone that adds a soft-delete-unique migration.
findings.fix: 1) In a test-only logging path, route Monolog + CI4 logs to a throwaway/null sink under CI_ENVIRONMENT=testing (PR #42 already does 'logger isolation' — land it). 2) Make LoggerFactory::getLogDirectory() honor an env override (e.g. write to sys_get_temp_dir() or /dev/null when ENVIRONMENT==='testing'). 3) Fix the migration: detect the SQLite autoindex name (or guard the dropKey behind a platform check / try existence) so it never emits a failing statement. 4) Lower Config\Logger::$threshold for the testing environment to <=4 (error) or route through a NullHandler. 5) Truncate the committed-working-tree logs locally.

findings.title: Two parallel logging stacks (CI4-native log-*.log + Monolog app-*.json) with only Monolog rotating
findings.evidence: writable/logs shows both families: log-2026-05-*.log (CI4 FileHandler, driven by app/Config/Logger.php) AND app-2026-05-*.json (Monolog via app/Infrastructure/Logging/LoggerFactory.php:90-100 RotatingFileHandler maxFiles=30). LoggerFactory rotates+caps at 30 files; the CI4-native .log stream has NO maxFiles cap in Logger.php and produced the 389MB single-day file. Both run simultaneously in the same process.
findings.impact: Cloned domains get two sources of truth for logs with divergent formats and retention. The MCP/AI tooling (.claude/documentation/LOGGING_BEST_PRACTICES.md) assumes the JSON stream, but exceptions land in the unbounded .log stream. Duplicate write cost on every request, and the uncapped .log stream is the disk-filler.
findings.fix: Pick one stack. Recommended: keep Monolog (JSON, rotating, redacting) as the only handler and disable the CI4-native FileHandler by trimming app/Config/Logger.php $handlers to a Monolog bridge (or set CI4 to delegate to PSR-3). If both must coexist, add maxFiles/rotation + a sane threshold to the CI4 handler. Document the single canonical path in LOGGING_BEST_PRACTICES.md.

findings.title: Duplicate test tree: PascalCase real suites + lowercase CI4-example stubs (tests/unit, _support, _skipped, session, database) shipped alongside
findings.evidence: tests/ contains BOTH Unit/ (real, 40+ dirs) and unit/ (only HealthTest.php); BOTH Support/ (5 files: IntegrationTestCase, FeatureTestCase, UnitTestCase, Factories) and _support/ (5 files: bootstrap_libraries.php, ExampleModel, ConfigReader, ExampleSeeder, a .php.bak migration); plus tests/_skipped/AbiSageIntacct (foreign Sage Intacct client leftover, 10+ files), tests/session/ExampleSessionTest.php, tests/database/ExampleDatabaseTest.php.bak. phpstan.neon:22-26 and phpcs.xml:34 explicitly exclude the lowercase trees as 'example stubs, not our project tests', and phpunit.xml.dist:30 excludes only _skipped. composer.json autoload-dev maps both Tests\Support\=>tests/Support and Tests\=>tests/.

The dual _support/Support split means new domains may extend the wrong (stub) base. Tooling-scope drift: every gate config must individually re-list the lowercase exclusions, and any new lowercase-pathed test silently escapes PHPStan/PHPCS.
findings.fix: Delete tests/unit, tests/_support, tests/_skipped, tests/session, tests/database, and the *.bak files; consolidate on tests/Unit, tests/Integration, tests/Feature, tests/Support. Remove the now-redundant exclude lines from phpstan.neon, phpcs.xml, phpunit.xml.dist. Keep one canonical UnitTestCase/IntegrationTestCase/FeatureTestCase. E18 is the natural home.

findings.title: app/Commands and app/Helpers are outside PHPStan scope and excluded from coverage denominator — ERP-critical relay/worker unchecked
findings.evidence: phpstan.neon:8-13 paths = app/Domain, Infrastructure, Libraries, Models, Controllers only — app/Commands and app/Helpers are NOT analyzed. phpunit.xml.dist <source> exclude (lines 42-67) drops app/Commands, app/Views, app/Config, Migrations, Seeds, Language plus specific adapters. app/Commands contains RelayOutboxEvents.php, WorkJobs.php, RebuildProjections.php — the outbox relay and job worker that ERP correctness depends on. app/Helpers/auth_ui_helper.php (the can()/current_actor() gates deptrac escape-hatches) is also unanalyzed.
findings.impact: The transactional-outbox relay and projection rebuild — the exact infrastructure every ERP domain leans on for eventual consistency — get neither PHPStan L8 nor the 90% coverage gate. The 90% number is computed on a denominator that excludes the riskiest async code. Cloned domains inherit unverified background processing.
findings.fix: Add app/Commands and app/Helpers to phpstan.neon paths (fix any L8 findings that surface). Move app/Commands out of the phpunit <source> exclude and write coverage for RelayOutboxEvents/WorkJobs (at least happy-path + retry). If some commands are genuinely thin CLI shells, keep them excluded but explicitly extract their logic into Infrastructure classes that ARE covered.

findings.title: IntegrationTestCase builds Cookie repos WITHOUT TenantContext, so tenant-scoping WHERE clause (most ERP-critical behavior) is never exercised by the base
findings.evidence: tests/Support/IntegrationTestCase.php:60-62 constructs `new CookieRepository($logger, $loggingConfig)` — no third TenantContext arg. CookieQueryRepository.php:229-232 makes the tenant filter a NO-OP when tenantContext===null ('legacy single-tenant tests, this is a no-op'); CookieRepository.php:458-459 only stamps tenant_id when tenantContext!==null. Production DOES inject it (ServiceProviderRegistry::resolveKnownDependency maps TenantContext->Services::tenantContext()), so the integration base tests a different code path than prod.
findings.impact: Cross-tenant isolation — the property that prevents ERP customer A from reading customer B's invoices — is validated only by whatever unit tests pass a context explicitly, not by the shared integration base every cloned domain inherits. A regression that drops the WHERE tenant_id clause would pass the integration suite. The reference entity ships its single most important guard untested at the base layer.
findings.fix: Have IntegrationTestCase construct repos WITH a TenantContext (default tenant 1) and add an explicit cross-tenant isolation test (seed tenant 1 + tenant 2, assert tenant-1 reads never return tenant-2 rows; assert save() stamps the active tenant). Make TenantContext a first-class, non-nullable repo dependency in the canonical pattern so cloners can't accidentally null it.

findings.title: DocumentNumberingService keys sequences on (series, scope) with no tenant_id — gapless numbers collide across tenants
findings.evidence: app/Infrastructure/Numbering/DocumentNumberingService.php:55-91 allocate() locks/queries document_sequences purely on (series, scope) (fetchOrCreateRow :151-153 WHERE series=? AND scope=?). No tenant_id column participates. The class is otherwise production-grade (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on MySQL/Postgres :141-148, transaction-wrapped, SQLite-aware).
findings.impact: In multi-tenant ERP, two tenants requesting series='invoice' share one counter unless every caller manually overloads `scope` with the tenant id — an easy-to-forget convention that, when missed, leaks one tenant's invoice volume to another and risks duplicate legal document numbers. This is the kind of subtle cross-tenant defect that compounds across every numbered ERP document (invoices, POs, credit notes).
findings.fix: Add tenant_id to the document_sequences migration + unique key (tenant_id, series, scope), inject TenantContext into DocumentNumberingService, and include tenant_id in the FOR UPDATE/WHERE/INSERT. Provide a documented escape for genuinely global series. Add a concurrency test (two tenants, same series, assert independent counters).

findings.title: app/Filters is empty while middleware lives in THREE infrastructure subdirs; deptrac Filters layer is vacuous
findings.evidence: `ls app/Filters/` returns nothing (empty). Middleware is split across app/Infrastructure/Auth/Middleware (6: Jwt, Permission, RateLimit, RoleAuthorization, SessionAuth, SessionRole), app/Infrastructure/Http/Middleware (1: Idempotency), and app/Infrastructure/Logging (CorrelationIdMiddleware). All are wired via aliases in app/Config/Filters.php:45-52, so none is dead — but deptrac.yaml defines a Filters layer (collector app/Filters/.*) and a Controllers->Filters rule that match zero classes.
findings.impact: A cloner asking 'where do filters go?' finds an empty canonical CI4 directory and three competing real homes, with no rule explaining which to use. The deptrac Filters layer gives false assurance it is governing a directory that is empty. New cross-cutting concerns will be placed inconsistently, and the Auth/ vs Http/ split has no principled boundary.
findings.fix: Pick ONE canonical home. Either (a) move all HTTP middleware to app/Filters (CI4-idiomatic) and update Config/Filters.php aliases + deptrac, or (b) formally retire app/Filters, delete the empty dir + its deptrac layer, and document app/Infrastructure/Http/Middleware as canonical with Auth-specific ones under Auth/Middleware. Document the rule in the scaffolding skill. E13 (provider/HTTP wiring) is the home.

findings.title: Soft-delete-unique migration pattern emits a failing dropKey('users_email') that every cloned domain will copy
findings.evidence: app/Database/Migrations/2026-05-20-210000_UsersEmailUniqueWithSoftDelete.php:39-43 wraps dropKey('users','users_email',false) in try/catch but the statement still reaches SQLite and throws the logged 'no such index: users_email' (see logging finding). The index name 'users_email' never existed on SQLite (the column-level UNIQUE autoindex has a different name). The author's own comment (:35-38) acknowledges the name varies by engine but the code still issues the failing drop.
findings.impact: This is the canonical 'replace global unique with composite soft-delete-aware unique' migration that cloners WILL copy for every ERP entity (the cookies table already uses the composite pattern). Each clone re-introduces the same failing-statement-logged-as-ERROR behavior, multiplying the log spam across domains.
findings.fix: Rewrite the pattern to be name-safe: on SQLite skip the drop entirely (the autoindex is a strictly-stronger backstop, as the docblock notes), and on MySQL query information_schema for the actual index name before dropping. Bake the corrected pattern into the scaffolding skill / property-addition protocol so clones inherit the safe version.

findings.title: Create-then-Drop CookieReadModel migration pair + no FKs on tenant_id/audit columns remain in canonical migration set
findings.evidence: Both app/Database/Migrations/2026-05-20-200000_CreateCookieReadModelTable.php and 2026-05-21-120000_DropCookieReadModelTable.php are present (RE-AUDIT-11 F4). CreateCookiesTable.php has tenant_id/created_by/updated_by/deleted_by columns but no addForeignKey (RE-AUDIT-11 F6). cookies.price is still DECIMAL(10,2) discarding the Currency the Money/CookiePrice VO carries (RE-AUDIT-11 F1, blocked on E09 not-yet-opened).
findings.impact: Cloners running `migrate --all` execute two no-op read-model migrations back-to-back and, on a single rollback, resurrect an orphaned table whose projection is only a .php.example. The money/currency mismatch is copied into every priced ERP entity. Missing FKs mean tenant/audit referential integrity is unenforced template-wide.
findings.fix: Squash the read-model Create/Drop pair into a single no-read-model end state (or delete both since the projection is .example). Open E09 to migrate cookies.price -> price_minor (INT/BIGINT) + price_currency (CHAR(3)). Add FKs (or a documented decision to omit them for sharding) to the canonical migration so clones inherit the choice consciously.

findings.title: pt-BR locale missing Validation.php entirely; cookie views hardcode English strings instead of lang() keys

Cookie views (app/Views/cookies/*.php) contain hardcoded literals ('Cancel', 'No description', etc.) with zero lang() calls observed in the esc-coverage scan. findings.title: A few dynamic view outputs (formattedPrice, numeric id) bypass esc(); name/description ARE escaped

supporting-sweep.erp_readiness_notes: Cross-cutting observations for cloning Cookie into real ERP domains: (1) TENANCY is the highest-leverage correctness property and it is currently OPT-IN via a nullable ctor arg — production injects it correctly through #[AutoBind], but tests don't, and DocumentNumberingService ignores it entirely.
